title: Septic arthritis
summary: Admit under pediatrics/orthopedics; septic child, hip/shoulder infection, delayed presentation or hemodynamic instability requires urgent operative and PICU planning.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit under pediatrics/orthopedics; septic child, hip/shoulder infection, delayed presentation or hemodynamic instability requires urgent operative and PICU planning.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, fever/pain, neurovascular checks and function; strict I&O if ill.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Supportive unless septic.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access; obtain cultures before antibiotics when stable, but do not delay in sepsis.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO until orthopedics determines aspiration/washout timing; isotonic IV fluids if intake poor or septic.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP/ESR, blood cultures; renal/liver tests for treatment baseline; aspirate/joint/bone cultures when obtained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent ultrasound for hip/effusion; radiograph for alternate pathology; MRI if adjacent osteomyelitis, deep joint or abscess is suspected.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Obtain blood and joint cultures promptly. Start cefazolin IV after aspiration when the child is stable and aspiration is imminent; do not delay antibiotics in sepsis. Use clindamycin/vancomycin for MRSA risk and broaden by age/exposure/local formulary.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Orthopedics urgently for aspiration/washout; ID for bacteremia, MRSA or complex disease.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: NPO, immobilize for comfort, neurovascular checks, pain scoring and specimen/culture tracking.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Serial joint pain/range of motion, fever, perfusion and CRP. Deterioration or persistent bacteremia/pain after source control requires urgent repeat orthopedic review.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Supportive unless septic.

Medications/treatments: Obtain blood and joint cultures promptly. Start cefazolin IV after aspiration when the child is stable and aspiration is imminent; do not delay antibiotics in sepsis. Use clindamycin/vancomycin for MRSA risk and broaden by age/exposure/local formulary.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Deep neck infection
summary: Admit to CTU/ward only if airway is stable with immediate senior/ENT review; use step-down/PICU when there is drooling, stridor, tripod positioning, trismus with progression, toxic appearance, mediastinal concern, or anticipated difficult airway.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward only if airway is stable with immediate senior/ENT review; use step-down/PICU when there is drooling, stridor, tripod positioning, trismus with progression, toxic appearance, mediastinal concern, or anticipated difficult airway.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; continuous observation if airway symptoms are present.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry; cardiorespiratory monitoring for airway risk, opioid use, or significant systemic illness. Keep airway equipment immediately available.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Keep the child calm and in a position of comfort; oxygen as tolerated. Do not force an oropharyngeal examination in a child with critical upper-airway signs.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain with experienced staff while minimizing distress; consider anesthetic/ENT support if access attempts may destabilize the airway.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO; isotonic IV fluids with reassessment for dehydration and sepsis.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP, electrolytes, blood culture if febrile/systemically unwell; operative cultures when drained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Contrast CT neck when stable enough and diagnosis/extent is uncertain; ultrasound for selected superficial disease; never delay airway control for imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start IV antibiotics covering oral flora, streptococci, staphylococci, and anaerobes per hospital pathway; analgesia; corticosteroid only after specialist discussion. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ENT urgently; anesthesia and PICU early for any airway concern; ID for severe/complicated disease; surgery for mediastinal extension.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Continuous airway observation, suction available, NPO signage, minimal agitation, and documentation of voice, drooling, neck position, swelling, and work of breathing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at bedside within 30-60 min and frequently thereafter; call anesthesia/PICU immediately for increasing stridor, fatigue, cyanosis, inability to handle secretions, altered mental status, or rapidly enlarging swelling.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Keep the child calm and in a position of comfort; oxygen as tolerated. Do not force an oropharyngeal examination in a child with critical upper-airway signs.

Medications/treatments: Start IV antibiotics covering oral flora, streptococci, staphylococci, and anaerobes per hospital pathway; analgesia; corticosteroid only after specialist discussion. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Bacteremia / positive blood culture callback
summary: Admit to CTU/ward if true bacteremia is likely, the child is young/high-risk, has an indwelling device, is clinically unwell, cannot ensure follow-up, or needs IV therapy; PICU for sepsis or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward if true bacteremia is likely, the child is young/high-risk, has an indwelling device, is clinically unwell, cannot ensure follow-up, or needs IV therapy; PICU for sepsis or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h depending on appearance and organism; use sepsis-frequency observations if unstable.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Clinical perfusion, mental status, urine output, fever curve; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if unwell.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As clinically indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain reliable access; repeat cultures before antibiotics when feasible, including each central-line lumen if present.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if stable; isotonic IV fluids only for poor intake or perfusion deficit.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat blood culture, CBC/differential, renal/liver function and source-directed tests; inflammatory markers if useful for trend. Confirm organism, time to positivity, number of positive bottles, and contamination likelihood.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed imaging only; consider echocardiography for selected organisms, persistent bacteremia, cardiac risk, or endocarditis concern after specialist review.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give organism- and source-appropriate empiric IV antibiotics after repeat cultures; narrow promptly when identification/susceptibility is known. Verify doses and allergies.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ID for S. aureus, fungal infection, persistent bacteremia, unusual organisms, hardware, endovascular concern, or uncertainty; relevant surgical service for source control.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Document exact culture details, antibiotic administration, line findings, fever, perfusion, urine output, and repeat-culture timing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess within 1h after arrival/therapy and review microbiology actively overnight; escalate for persistent positive cultures, shock, focal neurologic signs, new murmur, embolic findings, or device infection.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As clinically indicated.
Medications/treatments: Give organism- and source-appropriate empiric IV antibiotics after repeat cultures; narrow promptly when identification/susceptibility is known. Verify doses and allergies.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

IWK pediatric drug and clinical resources

title: Kawasaki disease
summary: Admit to CTU/ward with early cardiology/rheumatology or local KD-team involvement; PICU for shock, myocardial dysfunction, significant arrhythmia, or severe systemic inflammation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward with early cardiology/rheumatology or local KD-team involvement; PICU for shock, myocardial dysfunction, significant arrhythmia, or severe systemic inflammation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h for shock features, tachycardia out of proportion, or cardiac dysfunction.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, perfusion, fever curve; cardiorespiratory monitoring if myocardial involvement, shock, or arrhythmia concern.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as indicated; assess for pulmonary edema or pleural effusions in severe disease.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access before immunomodulatory therapy; consider additional access if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet as tolerated; cautious isotonic fluids if dehydrated, with reassessment for myocardial dysfunction and third spacing.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP/ESR, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, albumin, urinalysis; blood/urine cultures and additional infectious evaluation as indicated; cardiac biomarkers if myocardial involvement suspected.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG and echocardiogram per KD pathway; chest imaging only if respiratory/cardiac findings warrant it.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: After cardiology/senior review give IVIG 2 g/kg once plus aspirin according to current CPS/local pathway; treat ideally within 10 days of fever and later if persistent inflammation/coronary disease. Escalate IVIG-resistant or shock presentations with cardiology/rheumatology/PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology early; rheumatology/ID according to local model; PICU for shock or cardiac dysfunction.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Record exact fever times, mucocutaneous findings, perfusion, intake/output, infusion reactions, and aspirin/antiplatelet precautions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess during and after IVIG and at least q4h; urgent escalation for hypotension, gallop rhythm, respiratory distress, chest pain, arrhythmia, altered mental status, or persistent/recurrent fever after treatment window.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as indicated; assess for pulmonary edema or pleural effusions in severe disease.

Medications/treatments: After cardiology/senior review give IVIG 2 g/kg once plus aspirin according to current CPS/local pathway; treat ideally within 10 days of fever and later if persistent inflammation/coronary disease. Escalate IVIG-resistant or shock presentations with cardiology/rheumatology/PICU.

guidance: CPS: Kawasaki disease practical guidance (2026).

title: Acute mastoiditis
summary: Admit to ward for IV therapy; PICU for sepsis, altered mental status, venous sinus thrombosis, intracranial extension or airway compromise.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for IV therapy; PICU for sepsis, altered mental status, venous sinus thrombosis, intracranial extension or airway compromise.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h if febrile/toxic; frequent neurologic assessment with intracranial concern.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Pain, fever, postauricular swelling, pinna displacement and cranial nerve/neuro findings; continuous monitoring if septic.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support sepsis/airway as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Required for IV antibiotics/contrast imaging.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if no procedure planned; NPO when drainage/surgery may be required; isotonic IV fluids for poor intake.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP/ESR, blood culture if febrile/toxic; middle-ear/mastoid operative cultures when obtained.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Contrast CT temporal bones or MRI/MRV when severe, neurologic signs, suspected abscess, venous sinus thrombosis, intracranial complication or poor response; uncomplicated cases may be diagnosed clinically with ENT.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start IV ceftriaxone or ampicillin-sulbactam; add vancomycin for MRSA/severe/intracranial risk and metronidazole when anaerobic intracranial coverage is needed, per local formulary. Provide analgesia.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ENT urgently; ID for severe/complicated disease; neurosurgery/neurology/PICU for intracranial extension or thrombosis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess fever, pain, swelling and neuro status within 4-6 h and each shift. Worsening headache, vomiting, diplopia, focal deficit, persistent bacteremia or no improvement within 24-48 h requires imaging/source-control escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support sepsis/airway as needed.

Medications/treatments: Start IV ceftriaxone or ampicillin-sulbactam; add vancomycin for MRSA/severe/intracranial risk and metronidazole when anaerobic intracranial coverage is needed, per local formulary. Provide analgesia.

title: Influenza with hypoxemia or complications
summary: Admit to ward for hypoxemia, dehydration, significant comorbidity, bacterial coinfection, encephalopathy, myositis/rhabdomyolysis or inability to maintain care; PICU for respiratory failure, shock, myocarditis or severe neurologic disease.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for hypoxemia, dehydration, significant comorbidity, bacterial coinfection, encephalopathy, myositis/rhabdomyolysis or inability to maintain care; PICU for respiratory failure, shock, myocarditis or severe neurologic disease.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h based on severity; continuous monitoring while oxygen-dependent or significantly ill.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Respiratory status, hydration/urine output, mental status and muscle pain/weakness; cardiac monitoring for myocarditis/electrolyte abnormalities.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen, suction and escalation to HFNC/NIV per unit protocol; early PICU for rapid progression.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if dehydrated, hypoxemic, toxic or requiring IV therapy.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral/NG feeds as tolerated; isotonic IV fluids if needed, avoiding overload in pneumonia/myocarditis.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Viral PCR if it changes management/isolation; CBC, electrolytes/renal tests, CK/urinalysis for myositis, cultures and inflammatory markers for bacterial coinfection, troponin/BNP if cardiac concern.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for hypoxemia/focal findings/complication; cardiac/neuro imaging as indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start oseltamivir promptly for hospitalized influenza using age/weight/renal dosing; do not delay for test results when strongly suspected. Add empiric antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia/sepsis, especially S. aureus/GAS concern, based on severity/local guidance.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU for escalating support; ID for severe/antiviral resistance/immunocompromise; cardiology, neurology or nephrology for complications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Droplet/contact precautions per infection control; fever/pain control, hydration and urine-colour monitoring; document oxygen trajectory.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess q2-4h and after support changes. Rapid oxygen escalation, hemoptysis, shock, altered mental status, severe muscle pain with dark urine or cardiac signs requires complication-specific escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen, suction and escalation to HFNC/NIV per unit protocol; early PICU for rapid progression.

Medications/treatments: Start oseltamivir promptly for hospitalized influenza using age/weight/renal dosing; do not delay for test results when strongly suspected. Add empiric antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia/sepsis, especially S. aureus/GAS concern, based on severity/local guidance.

title: Invasive group A streptococcal infection / toxic shock
summary: Admit to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, necrotizing infection or toxin-mediated disease; stable bacteremia without shock still requires close monitored care and source evaluation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for shock, organ dysfunction, necrotizing infection or toxin-mediated disease; stable bacteremia without shock still requires close monitored care and source evaluation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous; BP/perfusion q5-15 min during resuscitation, then q1h.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry, hourly urine output, serial lactate, coagulation, renal/liver function and CK when myositis/necrotizing disease is possible.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen and early ventilatory support for respiratory failure; prepare for perioperative airway if source control is needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs/IO; arterial/central access with PICU as indicated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO. Balanced crystalloid 10-20 mL/kg aliquots with reassessment; move early to vasoactive support if fluid-refractory or fluid intolerant.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Blood and source cultures, CBC, gas/lactate, electrolytes, renal/liver tests, CK, coagulation/fibrinogen and type/crossmatch; repeat frequently.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed imaging only if it does not delay surgery; bedside assessment and operative exploration take priority for necrotizing infection.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give broad empiric sepsis coverage immediately, including a beta-lactam active against GAS plus clindamycin for toxin suppression; add MRSA/gram-negative/anaerobic coverage until source defined. Consider IVIG for refractory streptococcal toxic shock with ID/PICU. Urgent surgical debridement/source control is essential.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU, ID and surgery immediately; hematology/transfusion medicine for DIC/IVIG considerations.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Sepsis checklist, exact antibiotic/fluid/vasoactive times, mark skin changes, hourly urine output and preparation for repeated OR assessment.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes. Pain out of proportion, rapidly spreading edema/erythema, bullae, anesthesia, rising lactate/CK or persistent shock mandates immediate operative exploration and escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen and early ventilatory support for respiratory failure; prepare for perioperative airway if source control is needed.

Medications/treatments: Give broad empiric sepsis coverage immediately, including a beta-lactam active against GAS plus clindamycin for toxin suppression; add MRSA/gram-negative/anaerobic coverage until source defined. Consider IVIG for refractory streptococcal toxic shock with ID/PICU. Urgent surgical debridement/source control is essential.

title: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
summary: Admit to the hospital DKA pathway; PICU/step-down for severe DKA, cerebral-injury risk, hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, very young child, major electrolyte abnormality, or monitoring needs beyond the ward.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to the hospital DKA pathway; PICU/step-down for severe DKA, cerebral-injury risk, hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, very young child, major electrolyte abnormality, or monitoring needs beyond the ward.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1h with neurologic assessment throughout insulin therapy; temperature q4h; weight on admission and use the measured weight for calculations.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry; hourly glucose and neurologic checks; strict intake/output; document corrected sodium, fluid balance and Glasgow Coma Scale trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen only if needed; avoid routine bicarbonate. If consciousness declines, protect airway with PICU/anesthesia while avoiding hypocapnia from excessive ventilation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs if possible; do not delay initial fluid for a second line. Avoid central line unless necessary because of thrombosis risk.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO initially except ice chips if vomiting/altered. Give 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid 10-20 mL/kg over 20-30 min; additional 10 mL/kg boluses for shock with reassessment. Replace maintenance plus deficit over ~36 h per protocol; add dextrose when glucose falls to ~15-17 mmol/L or earlier if falling rapidly.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Initial glucose, VBG, sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, urea/creatinine, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, beta-hydroxybutyrate/ketones, osmolality if indicated; repeat glucose hourly and electrolytes/gas q2-4h per severity.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely. Neuroimaging must not delay treatment of suspected cerebral injury.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology early; PICU immediately for severe DKA, cerebral-injury signs, shock, refractory acidosis/electrolytes, or need for airway support; pharmacy for two-bag/insulin setup.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Use a DKA flowsheet; independent double-check insulin and fluids; hourly neuro/glucose documentation; do not give insulin bolus or bicarbonate without specialist direction.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review hourly glucose fall, sodium trend, perfusion and neuro status; adjust dextrose rather than stopping insulin. Headache, irritability, bradycardia, hypertension, vomiting, cranial nerve change or declining GCS = treat cerebral injury immediately.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen only if needed; avoid routine bicarbonate. If consciousness declines, protect airway with PICU/anesthesia while avoiding hypocapnia from excessive ventilation.

Medications/treatments: Start regular insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h after at least 1 h of fluids; no insulin bolus. Add potassium to IV fluids once urine output/renal function and serum potassium permit. For suspected cerebral injury give 3% saline 5 mL/kg over 10-15 min (max 250 mL) or mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg promptly and call PICU.

title: New-onset diabetes without DKA
summary: Admit to endocrinology/CTU when education cannot be completed safely as an outpatient, there is dehydration/ketosis, social or safeguarding concern, very young age, significant comorbidity, or unreliable follow-up; PICU only if DKA or critical metabolic instability develops.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to endocrinology/CTU when education cannot be completed safely as an outpatient, there is dehydration/ketosis, social or safeguarding concern, very young age, significant comorbidity, or unreliable follow-up; PICU only if DKA or critical metabolic instability develops.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h when stable; increase frequency for dehydration, vomiting, or evolving ketosis.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bedside glucose before meals, bedtime, overnight, and as symptoms dictate; ketones until cleared; strict I&O and daily weight.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for Kussmaul breathing or altered mental status suggesting evolving DKA.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routinely required if drinking and not acidotic; obtain if dehydrated, vomiting, or labs/IV therapy are needed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Encourage sugar-free fluids and regular carbohydrate-consistent meals per diabetes team; isotonic IV fluids for dehydration without using a DKA protocol unless criteria are met.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Confirm serum glucose, electrolytes, bicarbonate/venous gas, beta-hydroxybutyrate or ketones; HbA1c and diabetes classification labs per endocrinology; screen for associated autoimmune disease per pathway.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start subcutaneous insulin regimen with endocrinology using weight/age/puberty considerations; hypoglycemia orders and sick-day plan; verify all insulin doses independently.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology/diabetes educator, dietitian, nursing education, social work as needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Double-check insulin, carbohydrate intake, glucose/ketone documentation, injection teaching, device education, and hypoglycemia supplies.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess glucose/ketones after insulin and meals; convert immediately to DKA pathway and call senior/endocrinology if acidosis, persistent vomiting, rising ketones, worsening dehydration, or altered mental status appears.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for Kussmaul breathing or altered mental status suggesting evolving DKA.
Medications/treatments: Start subcutaneous insulin regimen with endocrinology using weight/age/puberty considerations; hypoglycemia orders and sick-day plan; verify all insulin doses independently.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Hypoglycemia
summary: Admit to ward for recurrent/persistent hypoglycemia, inability to maintain glucose orally, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, toxic ingestion, liver disease, or need for continuous dextrose; PICU for seizures, coma, high glucose-infusion requirement, or instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to ward for recurrent/persistent hypoglycemia, inability to maintain glucose orally, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, toxic ingestion, liver disease, or need for continuous dextrose; PICU for seizures, coma, high glucose-infusion requirement, or instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h when stable; q15-30 min during severe symptoms/resuscitation. Obtain an accurate weight.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bedside glucose every 15 min until corrected, then q30-60 min until stable and before feeds/overnight as directed; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if symptomatic or on high-concentration dextrose.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: ABC stabilization; oxygen and seizure management as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly for symptomatic/severe or recurrent hypoglycemia; IO if unstable. Central access may be needed for high dextrose concentration.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: If awake and safe, give rapid oral carbohydrate followed by complex carbohydrate/feed. If unable to take orally, give IV dextrose and continue glucose-containing isotonic fluids titrated to maintain target glucose.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Before treatment if this causes no delay, obtain critical sample at plasma glucose <=2.8 mmol/L: laboratory glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, free fatty acids, cortisol, growth hormone, lactate, ammonia, electrolytes, liver tests, acylcarnitine profile and urine organic acids/toxicology as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; targeted imaging only for suspected intracranial, hepatic, adrenal or ingestion-related cause.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat immediately. Common IV rescue is D10W 2-5 mL/kg (institution/age dependent), then glucose infusion adjusted to response. If no IV, glucagon IM/SC may be used according to age/weight and available product. For neonates, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally may be used with a feed when appropriate.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology/metabolic genetics for unexplained, ketotic/non-ketotic recurrent hypoglycemia or high glucose requirement; toxicology for ingestion; PICU for neurologic compromise or escalating dextrose.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Treat based on bedside result but send confirmatory laboratory glucose; document symptoms, treatment, feeding and response; never leave an infant/child fasting without a glucose plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Recheck in 15 min after each rescue. Repeat rescue/escalate infusion if still low. Inability to maintain target despite glucose infusion, absent ketones, hepatomegaly, acidosis, hyperammonemia or recurrent overnight lows requires urgent specialist review.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: ABC stabilization; oxygen and seizure management as required.

Medications/treatments: Treat immediately. Common IV rescue is D10W 2-5 mL/kg (institution/age dependent), then glucose infusion adjusted to response. If no IV, glucagon IM/SC may be used according to age/weight and available product. For neonates, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally may be used with a feed when appropriate.

title: Adrenal crisis
summary: Admit to step-down/PICU if shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, altered mental status or repeated hypoglycemia; otherwise monitored ward care after stabilization.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to step-down/PICU if shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, altered mental status or repeated hypoglycemia; otherwise monitored ward care after stabilization.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q15-30 min during resuscitation, then q1-2h until stable and q4h thereafter; weight for dosing.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring for shock/hyperkalemia; frequent glucose, neurologic/perfusion assessment and strict intake/output.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; altered mental status may reflect shock, hypoglycemia or severe sodium disturbance.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs or IO immediately if unstable; do not delay hydrocortisone for testing or access difficulty.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Give 0.9% saline 20 mL/kg rapidly for shock (smaller aliquots if cardiac/renal concern), repeat to perfusion; add dextrose for hypoglycemia and continue isotonic glucose-containing maintenance/deficit fluids.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Draw cortisol and ACTH before steroid only if this will not delay treatment; glucose, electrolytes, gas, urea/creatinine, CBC and cultures if infection suspected. Repeat sodium, potassium and glucose frequently.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; investigate precipitating illness as indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Hydrocortisone 100 mg/m2 IV/IM immediately (max 100 mg); practical emergency doses: infant 25 mg, child <15 kg 50 mg, child >=15 kg 100 mg. Continue 30-50 mg/m2/day divided q6h IV (or q8h IM) and taper with endocrinology once stable.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology urgently; PICU for shock, severe electrolyte disturbance or neurologic compromise; infectious disease/other services for precipitating illness.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Give steroid before nonessential investigations; document emergency dose/time; maintain stress-dose plan and medical-alert information; monitor for fluid overload and potassium change.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess perfusion and glucose within 10-15 min, electrolytes within 1-2 h. Persistent shock after fluids/hydrocortisone requires PICU, vasoactive support and search for sepsis/hemorrhage.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support as required; altered mental status may reflect shock, hypoglycemia or severe sodium disturbance.

Medications/treatments: Hydrocortisone 100 mg/m2 IV/IM immediately (max 100 mg); practical emergency doses: infant 25 mg, child <15 kg 50 mg, child >=15 kg 100 mg. Continue 30-50 mg/m2/day divided q6h IV (or q8h IM) and taper with endocrinology once stable.

guidance: CPS/Canadian endocrine emergency guidance.

title: Hyponatremia / SIADH
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic, moderate/severe, rapidly falling, or etiologically unclear hyponatremia; PICU for seizure, altered mental status, respiratory compromise, severe symptoms, or need for hypertonic saline infusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic, moderate/severe, rapidly falling, or etiologically unclear hyponatremia; PICU for seizure, altered mental status, respiratory compromise, severe symptoms, or need for hypertonic saline infusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h when stable; continuous observation during acute correction or neurologic symptoms.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, neurologic checks, and fluid balance; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring for severe/symptomatic cases.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure or encephalopathy; avoid free water.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; two lines if severe symptoms or hypertonic therapy is anticipated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Stop hypotonic fluids. Use isotonic maintenance for most hospitalized children when appropriate; fluid restrict for SIADH after volume status is established; treat hypovolemia carefully.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat serum sodium at a frequency matched to severity/correction; serum osmolality, glucose, urea/creatinine, urine sodium/osmolality, and cause-directed endocrine/renal tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; neuroimaging if focal deficits, trauma, suspected CNS pathology, or unexplained severe symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Symptomatic severe hyponatremia requires hypertonic saline per emergency/PICU pathway; treat the underlying cause and prevent overly rapid correction. Verify concentration and calculations with pharmacy.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU for symptoms/severe level; nephrology/endocrinology for complex, recurrent, renal, or endocrine causes; neurology if seizures/CNS disease.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Exact intake/output, no unapproved free water, double-check fluid sodium concentration/rate, and draw timed sodium levels.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess neurologic status and sodium closely during correction; escalate for seizure, declining GCS, respiratory change, rising sodium faster than target, or inability to control fluid balance.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure or encephalopathy; avoid free water.

Medications/treatments: Symptomatic severe hyponatremia requires hypertonic saline per emergency/PICU pathway; treat the underlying cause and prevent overly rapid correction. Verify concentration and calculations with pharmacy.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Hypernatremia
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for significant hypernatremia, dehydration, neurologic symptoms, unreliable enteral replacement, or uncertain chronicity; PICU for severe symptoms, shock, seizures, or need for very frequent laboratory correction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for significant hypernatremia, dehydration, neurologic symptoms, unreliable enteral replacement, or uncertain chronicity; PICU for severe symptoms, shock, seizures, or need for very frequent laboratory correction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h; more frequently if shock, neurologic symptoms, or active rapid changes.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily or more frequent weight, neurologic checks, and careful cumulative fluid balance; cardiorespiratory monitoring if severe.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support as indicated; seizure precautions for severe hypernatremia.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second access if shock or frequent sampling is needed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Restore intravascular volume first with isotonic fluid when shocked, then replace free-water deficit gradually using a calculated plan; include ongoing losses and avoid overly rapid correction.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Serial sodium, glucose, urea/creatinine, potassium, bicarbonate, osmolality; urine studies and endocrine/renal testing when diabetes insipidus or renal loss is possible.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; neuroimaging for focal findings, trauma, or unexplained severe neurologic symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the cause, replace deficits gradually, and correct concurrent glucose/electrolyte abnormalities; verify calculations and fluid composition with senior/pharmacy.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology/endocrinology for severe, recurrent, DI-related, renal, or complex cases; PICU for neurologic symptoms or shock.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Accurate hourly intake/output in severe cases, timed weights/labs, and independent double-check of fluid composition/rate.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess sodium trend and neurologic status at each laboratory interval; escalate for seizure, cerebral edema concern, worsening shock, oliguria, or correction outside the planned rate.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support as indicated; seizure precautions for severe hypernatremia.
Medications/treatments: Treat the cause, replace deficits gradually, and correct concurrent glucose/electrolyte abnormalities; verify calculations and fluid composition with senior/pharmacy.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Hyperkalemia
summary: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for ECG changes, severe elevation, rapid rise, renal failure with oliguria/anuria, hemodynamic instability, or need for repeated temporizing therapy/dialysis.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for ECG changes, severe elevation, rapid rise, renal failure with oliguria/anuria, hemodynamic instability, or need for repeated temporizing therapy/dialysis.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until potassium and ECG are stable, then space cautiously.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring; strict I&O; repeat ECG after treatment or any rhythm change.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As needed; prepare resuscitation equipment if ECG changes or instability are present.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Immediate reliable IV access; second line if severe. Confirm a non-hemolyzed sample without delaying treatment when ECG changes are present.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Stop potassium-containing fluids/feeds and offending medications; manage volume status and glucose carefully.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat potassium, glucose, blood gas/bicarbonate, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, urea/creatinine; CK/uric acid and hemolysis/tumor-lysis studies when indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routinely required; renal ultrasound for obstruction or selected renal causes.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. With ECG change or severe hyperkalemia give calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV (max 10 mL) with monitoring; shift potassium with regular insulin 0.1 units/kg IV plus dextrose, nebulized salbutamol and bicarbonate only for significant acidosis. Remove potassium with diuretic/resin/dialysis as appropriate; use local emergency protocol and pharmacy double check.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology urgently for renal failure, refractory hyperkalemia, or dialysis concern; PICU for ECG changes/instability; oncology if tumor lysis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Continuous rhythm observation, immediate reporting of ECG changes, frequent glucose checks after insulin-based therapy, strict I&O, and timed repeat potassium.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess ECG and potassium within the pathway-defined interval after each intervention; escalate for bradycardia, QRS widening, ventricular arrhythmia, recurrent rise, hypoglycemia, or oliguria/anuria.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed; prepare resuscitation equipment if ECG changes or instability are present.

Medications/treatments: Stop potassium sources. With ECG change or severe hyperkalemia give calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV (max 10 mL) with monitoring; shift potassium with regular insulin 0.1 units/kg IV plus dextrose, nebulized salbutamol and bicarbonate only for significant acidosis. Remove potassium with diuretic/resin/dialysis as appropriate; use local emergency protocol and pharmacy double check.

title: Hypocalcemia
summary: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic or significant hypocalcemia, prolonged QT, seizure/tetany, or unclear cause; PICU for arrhythmia, airway compromise, recurrent seizure, or continuous IV calcium requirement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward for symptomatic or significant hypocalcemia, prolonged QT, seizure/tetany, or unclear cause; PICU for arrhythmia, airway compromise, recurrent seizure, or continuous IV calcium requirement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h; continuous observation during IV replacement.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Cardiac monitoring for symptomatic disease or IV calcium; seizure precautions and neurologic checks; strict I&O when renal disease is possible.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure, laryngospasm, or severe tetany.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; verify patency carefully for IV calcium because extravasation can cause injury.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if safe; correct associated magnesium deficiency and address phosphate/vitamin D intake according to cause.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Ionized and total calcium, albumin, magnesium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D, renal function, blood gas; ECG and cause-directed tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Cause-directed only; consider skeletal imaging for rickets or renal imaging when indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Symptomatic/severe hypocalcemia: calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV slowly (max 10-20 mL per local protocol) with ECG and secure IV-site monitoring; correct magnesium and cause. Oral calcium/calcitriol for stable cases with endocrinology/nephrology guidance.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Endocrinology for unclear/recurrent disease; nephrology for renal causes; cardiology for persistent QT/arrhythmia; genetics if syndromic concern.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Cardiac monitoring, IV-site checks during calcium infusion, seizure precautions, and timed repeat ionized calcium/magnesium.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess symptoms, ECG, and ionized calcium after treatment; escalate for laryngospasm, seizure, ventricular arrhythmia, refractory low calcium, or infusion extravasation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation during seizure, laryngospasm, or severe tetany.

Medications/treatments: Symptomatic/severe hypocalcemia: calcium gluconate 10% 0.5-1 mL/kg IV slowly (max 10-20 mL per local protocol) with ECG and secure IV-site monitoring; correct magnesium and cause. Oral calcium/calcitriol for stable cases with endocrinology/nephrology guidance.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
summary: Admit for significant mucosal bleeding, severe headache/neuro symptoms, hemodynamic concern, inability to ensure follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty or treatment requiring observation; isolated skin findings with well child are often outpatient after hematology discussion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for significant mucosal bleeding, severe headache/neuro symptoms, hemodynamic concern, inability to ensure follow-up, diagnostic uncertainty or treatment requiring observation; isolated skin findings with well child are often outpatient after hematology discussion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding checks and neuro observations when platelets are very low or headache/head trauma is present; avoid unnecessary continuous monitoring.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support if major hemorrhage.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Avoid unnecessary venipuncture; IV access if treatment/bleeding.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral as tolerated; blood products only for defined indication with hematology input.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC with manual smear and reticulocytes; repeat count to exclude clumping. Additional coagulation, hemolysis, viral or marrow studies only for atypical features. Typical ITP has isolated thrombocytopenia with otherwise reassuring smear.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent head CT for neurologic symptoms/significant head trauma; otherwise no routine imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat bleeding rather than platelet count alone. For non-life-threatening mucosal bleeding use prednisone/prednisolone or IVIG per hematology pathway. Life-threatening bleeding: IVIG plus high-dose corticosteroid plus platelet transfusion with hematology/PICU. Avoid NSAIDs/IM injections.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology early for treatment, atypical features or severe count; PICU/neurosurgery for intracranial bleed; gynecology for uncontrolled uterine bleeding.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Bleeding precautions, soft toothbrush, avoid rectal temperatures/IM injections/contact activity; quantify menstrual/GI/urine bleeding.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess bleeding and neuro status frequently. New severe headache, vomiting, focal deficit, major GI/GU bleeding or hemodynamic change requires immediate hematology/PICU and critical-bleeding treatment.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support if major hemorrhage.

Medications/treatments: Treat bleeding rather than platelet count alone. For non-life-threatening mucosal bleeding use prednisone/prednisolone or IVIG per hematology pathway. Life-threatening bleeding: IVIG plus high-dose corticosteroid plus platelet transfusion with hematology/PICU. Avoid NSAIDs/IM injections.

title: Thrombocytopenia - not typical ITP
summary: Admit for active bleeding, platelet trend rapidly falling, additional cytopenias, abnormal smear, systemic illness, suspected TMA/DIC/leukemia, neonatal alloimmune disease or uncertain follow-up; PICU for major hemorrhage or shock.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for active bleeding, platelet trend rapidly falling, additional cytopenias, abnormal smear, systemic illness, suspected TMA/DIC/leukemia, neonatal alloimmune disease or uncertain follow-up; PICU for major hemorrhage or shock.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals; bleeding checks; neuro observations when severe thrombocytopenia/headache/head trauma; avoid unnecessary continuous monitors unless unstable.

sections.label: Respiratory support

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Avoid unnecessary venipuncture; IV access if treatment/bleeding.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral as tolerated; blood products only for defined indication with hematology input.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC in citrate tube if clumping, manual smear, reticulocytes, coagulation/fibrinogen, hemolysis panel, renal/liver tests and infection studies guided by context. Blasts, schistocytes or pancytopenia require urgent specialist review.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging; urgent head CT for neurologic symptoms/significant head injury; source-directed imaging for internal bleeding.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the cause. Platelet transfusion thresholds depend on bleeding, procedure and diagnosis; do not transfuse prophylactically in typical ITP or TTP/HUS without specialist direction unless life-threatening bleeding.

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Trend platelets/bleeding and organ function. Neurologic symptoms, renal failure, hemolysis, coagulopathy or systemic deterioration requires urgent syndrome-specific escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support if major hemorrhage.

title: Reactive leukocytosis
summary: Admit only for the underlying illness, inability to exclude serious infection/inflammation, marked persistent count with concerning symptoms/smear, or unreliable follow-up; leukocytosis alone is not an admission diagnosis.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit only for the underlying illness, inability to exclude serious infection/inflammation, marked persistent count with concerning symptoms/smear, or unreliable follow-up; leukocytosis alone is not an admission diagnosis.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals and monitoring dictated by cause; cardiorespiratory/neuro monitoring for hyperleukocytosis; strict I&O if tumor lysis management.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: As clinically indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if ill or urgent workup.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Cause-directed; tumor lysis fluids only under oncology/local protocol.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC/differential when needed, manual smear, CRP/ESR and cause-directed studies. Look for toxic change versus blasts, basophilia, cytopenias or hemolysis.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed; CXR if mediastinal mass symptoms but avoid sedating/supine procedures in suspected anterior mediastinal mass until expert plan.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the underlying cause; do not give antibiotics or steroids solely for a high WBC. Avoid steroids before leukemia is excluded when blasts/mediastinal mass are possible.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology for blasts, unexplained WBC >50-100 x10^9/L, persistent abnormalities or additional cytopenias.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Flag possible mediastinal mass precautions; track neurologic/respiratory symptoms and urine output.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review smear promptly. Respiratory/neuro symptoms, blasts, tumor-lysis abnormalities or WBC >=100 x10^9/L should be managed as hyperleukocytosis, not reactive leukocytosis.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: As clinically indicated.

title: Hyperleukocytosis / leukostasis concern
summary: Admit directly to PICU/oncology-capable monitored setting for WBC >=100 x10^9/L with suspected leukemia or any respiratory, neurologic, visual, renal or priapism symptoms; avoid routine ward placement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit directly to PICU/oncology-capable monitored setting for WBC >=100 x10^9/L with suspected leukemia or any respiratory, neurologic, visual, renal or priapism symptoms; avoid routine ward placement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous monitoring; q1h neurologic, respiratory and perfusion assessments initially.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry, strict intake/output, daily weights; serial tumor-lysis labs q4-6h or more frequently when unstable.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; avoid unnecessary sedation/intubation in a possible anterior mediastinal mass—call anesthesia/PICU/oncology before airway intervention whenever possible.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two peripheral IVs; avoid central line/procedural sedation until mediastinal mass and coagulopathy are assessed. Do not delay treatment if access is difficult.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Begin carefully monitored isotonic hydration for tumor-lysis prevention unless fluid overloaded; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids initially. Avoid red-cell transfusion before hematology review because viscosity may worsen leukostasis.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC/differential and urgent manual smear, electrolytes, creatinine, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, LDH, coagulation/fibrinogen, type and screen; blood gas/lactate if unstable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent chest radiograph before sedation/central access to assess mediastinal mass; neuroimaging only for symptoms and after stabilization.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start tumor-lysis prophylaxis/treatment with hematology—rasburicase for high risk/raised uric acid or allopurinol for selected lower risk. Cytoreduction (steroid, hydroxyurea, chemotherapy or leukapheresis) is hematology-directed. Treat fever as febrile neutropenia/sepsis.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology/oncology and PICU immediately; anesthesia if airway/procedure; nephrology for severe tumor lysis/renal failure.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Minimize exertion, maintain accurate fluid balance, avoid potassium/phosphate supplementation and nonessential transfusion, institute tumor-lysis lab schedule and bleeding precautions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess neuro/respiratory status hourly. New headache, confusion, focal deficit, hypoxemia, chest pain, priapism, oliguria or rising potassium/phosphate/uric acid requires immediate cytoreduction/PICU response.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; avoid unnecessary sedation/intubation in a possible anterior mediastinal mass—call anesthesia/PICU/oncology before airway intervention whenever possible.

Medications/treatments: Start tumor-lysis prophylaxis/treatment with hematology—rasburicase for high risk/raised uric acid or allopurinol for selected lower risk. Cytoreduction (steroid, hydroxyurea, chemotherapy or leukapheresis) is hematology-directed. Treat fever as febrile neutropenia/sepsis.

title: Anemia
summary: Admit to Ward if stable; PICU/resuscitation area for shock, active major bleeding, severe hypoxemia/heart failure, rapidly falling hemoglobin or transfusion reaction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if stable; PICU/resuscitation area for shock, active major bleeding, severe hypoxemia/heart failure, rapidly falling hemoglobin or transfusion reaction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, perfusion and symptom checks; cardiorespiratory monitoring during transfusion or if severe; strict I&O when heart/renal compromise.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if symptomatic, active bleeding or transfusion likely.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Avoid indiscriminate boluses; resuscitate hemorrhagic shock with blood-product strategy under senior guidance.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/indices, reticulocytes, smear; type and screen/crossmatch; bilirubin/LDH/haptoglobin/DAT for hemolysis; ferritin/iron studies when appropriate; coagulation and source tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed imaging for bleeding; ultrasound for splenic concern; do not delay stabilization.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat cause. RBC transfusion decision depends on symptoms, chronicity, hemodynamics and local threshold; use weight-based aliquot and slower rate in chronic severe anemia/heart failure risk. Treat iron deficiency only after appropriate assessment.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology for severe/atypical/hemolytic/marrow failure; surgery/GI/gynecology for bleeding source; PICU for instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Baseline and transfusion vitals, reaction monitoring, quantify bleeding, avoid repeated phlebotomy.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess continuously if bleeding; after transfusion per policy and clinical response; repeat CBC timing based on stability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as required.

title: Febrile neutropenia - oncology or immunocompromised
summary: Admit to oncology/CTU after immediate febrile-neutropenia pathway is started; PICU for sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, altered mental status, or other organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to oncology/CTU after immediate febrile-neutropenia pathway is started; PICU for sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, altered mental status, or other organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Frequent vitals; continuous monitoring if unwell; strict I&O; avoid rectal temperatures/exams.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access promptly. Obtain blood cultures from each central-line lumen and a peripheral culture when required by the hospital pathway; do not delay antibiotics for difficult access.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral/IV as indicated; bolus only for perfusion deficit.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, cultures, renal/liver function; urinalysis/culture and viral testing/source labs as indicated; lactate/coagulation if ill.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: CXR only for respiratory findings; source-directed imaging; consider fungal evaluation for persistent/prolonged fever with oncology/ID.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give first antipseudomonal beta-lactam within 60 min—commonly piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime or meropenem according to oncology pathway. Add vancomycin only for hemodynamic instability, suspected line/skin infection, pneumonia, MRSA or other defined indication. Do not delay for ANC confirmation in an unstable child.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consult oncology immediately; involve ID for persistent fever, resistant organisms, invasive fungal concern, or a complex source; call PICU for instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Neutropenic precautions per policy; no rectal meds/temperatures; meticulous line care; record exact antibiotic time.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess within 30–60 minutes after antibiotics/fluids and at least q2–4 h; review cultures and fever trajectory.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

title: Fever with neutropenia - presumed immunocompetent child
summary: Admit to CTU/ward if ill-appearing, age/risk factors fall outside the low-risk CPS population, severe neutropenia with concerning features, bacterial source, unreliable follow-up, or evolving sepsis; PICU for instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/ward if ill-appearing, age/risk factors fall outside the low-risk CPS population, severe neutropenia with concerning features, bacterial source, unreliable follow-up, or evolving sepsis; PICU for instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; sepsis-frequency observations if unwell.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Clinical appearance, perfusion, fever curve, urine output; continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring only when clinically indicated.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if ill-appearing, antibiotics/fluids are required, or follow-up risk is high; well-appearing low-risk children may not require IV access.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Encourage oral intake; isotonic IV fluids only for dehydration or perfusion deficit.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC/differential and smear; blood culture when ANC is severely reduced or risk factors are present; source-directed urine/viral/other tests. Review prior CBCs and medications.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed only; no routine chest radiograph without respiratory findings.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Ill-appearing or high-risk children receive empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics per sepsis/hospital pathway. Well-appearing, first-episode, otherwise healthy children may be observed without empiric antibiotics when CPS low-risk criteria are met.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology for persistent, recurrent, severe, multilineage, abnormal smear, or malignancy concern; ID for unusual infection; PICU for instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Avoid rectal temperatures/examinations in severe neutropenia; document fever, appearance, oral intake, and exact follow-up plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess within 1-2h and review CBC trend; escalate for worsening appearance, new focal infection, hypotension, persistent fever with severe neutropenia, or additional cytopenias/blasts.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed.

title: Pancytopenia / suspected leukemia
summary: Admit to CTU/hematology-oncology; PICU for hyperleukocytosis symptoms, tumor lysis, severe bleeding, sepsis, respiratory compromise, or neurologic changes.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/hematology-oncology; PICU for hyperleukocytosis symptoms, tumor lysis, severe bleeding, sepsis, respiratory compromise, or neurologic changes.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; more frequently for fever, bleeding, cardiorespiratory symptoms, or tumor-lysis risk.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding, perfusion, fever, neurologic/respiratory symptoms, strict I&O; cardiac monitoring if electrolyte abnormalities or tumor lysis are present.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as indicated; avoid unnecessary sedation in hyperleukocytosis or mediastinal-mass concern.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain carefully; avoid central-line placement until oncology plan and coagulation/platelets are reviewed unless emergent.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Maintain hydration according to tumor-lysis risk and cardiac/renal status; regular diet if safe; avoid potassium/phosphate load when TLS is possible.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Repeat CBC/differential, manual smear, reticulocytes, coagulation/fibrinogen, electrolytes, renal/liver function, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, LDH, type and screen; cultures if febrile.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for mediastinal mass symptoms or suspected leukemia/lymphoma; additional imaging only with oncology. Avoid sedation if anterior mediastinal mass is possible.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat fever as high-risk when neutropenic; initiate tumor-lysis prophylaxis/treatment with oncology; transfuse only after hematology review unless life-threatening instability. Verify products and doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology-oncology urgently; PICU for organ compromise; anesthesia before any sedation with mediastinal-mass concern; transfusion medicine as needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Bleeding precautions, no rectal procedures, infection precautions per policy, strict fluid balance, and prompt reporting of dyspnea, headache, visual change, priapism, or new bleeding.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess labs and symptoms at the interval set by oncology/TLS risk; escalate for rising potassium/uric acid/phosphate, falling calcium, oliguria, hypoxemia, neurologic change, or major bleeding.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as indicated; avoid unnecessary sedation in hyperleukocytosis or mediastinal-mass concern.

summary: Admit to Ward for uncomplicated pain with stable oxygenation; PICU for acute chest with severe support, stroke, shock, multiorgan failure or severe sequestration.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for uncomplicated pain with stable oxygenation; PICU for acute chest with severe support, stroke, shock, multiorgan failure or severe sequestration.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Pain/sedation and respiratory scoring; pulse oximetry while hypoxemic, receiving escalating opioids or chest symptoms; incentive spirometry; strict I&O.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Incentive spirometry while awake; oxygen to baseline/target if hypoxemic; early mobilization.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access if parenteral medications/fluids; avoid repeated traumatic attempts—use vascular-access support.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral hydration preferred; isotonic maintenance at no more than necessary; avoid fluid overload.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/retic and type/screen if severe/atypical, fever, pallor, chest symptoms or possible transfusion; cultures for fever; renal/liver tests as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: CXR for chest pain, cough, fever, hypoxemia or respiratory signs; targeted imaging for alternate diagnosis.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start analgesia within 30 min: acetaminophen/NSAID when safe plus opioid for moderate-severe pain using the individualized plan; reassess and repeat/titrate every 20-30 min until controlled. sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology for admission/complication; pain team for difficult control; PICU/neurology for stroke; urology for priapism.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Use pain and sedation scores; incentive spirometry typically q2 h while awake per hospital pathway; monitor bowel/bladder and mobility.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess analgesia within 15–30 minutes after IV opioid and at each dose; evaluate new fever, chest or neuro symptoms immediately.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Incentive spirometry while awake; oxygen to baseline/target if hypoxemic; early mobilization.

summary: Admit to CTU/hematology with early PICU awareness. Use PICU/step-down for hypoxemia, multilobar disease, rapidly increasing work of breathing, falling hemoglobin or platelet count, altered mental status, or need for HFNC/NIV.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/hematology with early PICU awareness. Use PICU/step-down for hypoxemia, multilobar disease, rapidly increasing work of breathing, falling hemoglobin or platelet count, altered mental status, or need for HFNC/NIV.

sections.label: Respiratory support

title: Splenic sequestration / acute anemia in sickle cell disease
summary: Admit to hematology/CTU; PICU for shock, severe anemia with cardiovascular compromise, altered mental status, respiratory distress, or rapidly enlarging spleen.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to hematology/CTU; PICU for shock, severe anemia with cardiovascular compromise, altered mental status, respiratory distress, or rapidly enlarging spleen.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until perfusion and hemoglobin are stable, then space cautiously.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if unstable or transfusing; serial spleen size, perfusion, mental status, urine output, and pain.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen for hypoxemia or shock; assess simultaneously for acute chest syndrome.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two reliable IVs when unstable or transfusion is anticipated; obtain type and cross urgently.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Isotonic resuscitation only as needed for shock while preparing blood; avoid excessive crystalloid dilution. NPO if unstable.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/reticulocytes, type and cross, bilirubin/hemolysis markers, electrolytes/renal function; cultures and chest radiograph if febrile or respiratory symptoms.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine splenic imaging when clinical diagnosis is clear; ultrasound if anatomy/diagnosis is uncertain and the child is stable.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Urgent packed RBC transfusion using hematology guidance and cautious target to avoid hyperviscosity; analgesia; treat concurrent infection/ACS. Verify product specifications and volume.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology immediately; PICU for shock; transfusion medicine; surgery only for selected recurrent/refractory cases.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Mark/measure spleen edge, document perfusion and transfusion response, monitor for reaction, and avoid delay in blood administration once ordered.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess continuously during resuscitation/transfusion and repeat CBC as directed; escalate for persistent shock, increasing spleen size, worsening anemia, respiratory symptoms, or transfusion reaction.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen for hypoxemia or shock; assess simultaneously for acute chest syndrome.

Medications/treatments: Urgent packed RBC transfusion using hematology guidance and cautious target to avoid hyperviscosity; analgesia; treat concurrent infection/ACS. Verify product specifications and volume.
