title: Bleeding disorder / hemophilia
summary: Admit to hematology/CTU for significant bleeding, head/neck/abdominal trauma, joint/muscle bleed impairing function, need for repeated factor, uncertain diagnosis, or inability to monitor at home; PICU for intracranial, airway, hemodynamic, or compartment compromise.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to hematology/CTU for significant bleeding, head/neck/abdominal trauma, joint/muscle bleed impairing function, need for repeated factor, uncertain diagnosis, or inability to monitor at home; PICU for intracranial, airway, hemodynamic, or compartment compromise.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; more frequently with active bleeding or after major trauma.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding site, neurovascular status, pain, circumference/swelling, urine/stool, neurologic checks after head injury; cardiorespiratory monitoring if unstable.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As needed; airway bleeding requires immediate anesthesia/ENT/PICU involvement.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly but minimize traumatic attempts; use prolonged pressure after venipuncture. Do not delay factor replacement for imaging.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet if safe; NPO for possible procedure; isotonic fluids/blood products for hemodynamic compromise.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, type and screen, PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen and factor/inhibitor testing as directed. Normal coagulation tests do not exclude every bleeding disorder.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Immediate CT for significant head injury/symptoms after factor is started; ultrasound/MRI for selected muscle/joint bleeds; source-directed imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give the patient-specific factor concentrate or hemostatic agent immediately per bleeding-disorder card/hematology plan; antifibrinolytic for selected mucosal bleeding; avoid NSAIDs/IM injections. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology immediately; neurosurgery/trauma/surgery for critical bleeding; ENT/dentistry for mucosal source; PICU for instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Bleeding precautions, pressure after procedures, neurovascular checks, factor administration documentation, and avoidance of rectal/IM procedures.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after factor and repeat level/labs when directed; urgent escalation for headache, vomiting, focal deficit, airway symptoms, expanding muscle bleed, compartment signs, hematuria with obstruction, or shock.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed; airway bleeding requires immediate anesthesia/ENT/PICU involvement.

Medications/treatments: Give the patient-specific factor concentrate or hemostatic agent immediately per bleeding-disorder card/hematology plan; antifibrinolytic for selected mucosal bleeding; avoid NSAIDs/IM injections. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Tumor lysis syndrome
summary: Admit to oncology with monitored/step-down capability; PICU for arrhythmia, severe electrolyte disturbance, oliguria/anuria, seizure, fluid overload, or anticipated renal replacement therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to oncology with monitored/step-down capability; PICU for arrhythmia, severe electrolyte disturbance, oliguria/anuria, seizure, fluid overload, or anticipated renal replacement therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h during active instability, then q2-4h once controlled.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring, strict hourly I&O, frequent weights, fluid balance, neurologic status, and signs of pulmonary edema.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; avoid fluid overload and prepare for escalation if pulmonary edema develops.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable access, often two lines; central access only with oncology plan and procedural safety review.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Start oncology-directed IV hydration; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids and unnecessary calcium; adjust for cardiac/renal status.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Frequent potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, LDH, magnesium; ECG and urinalysis. Frequency is based on TLS risk and active abnormalities.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routinely required; renal ultrasound if obstruction is suspected; chest imaging for pulmonary edema/mediastinal mass concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Uric-acid lowering therapy and electrolyte treatment per oncology/TLS pathway; treat hyperkalemia emergently; avoid routine calcium for asymptomatic hypocalcemia with high phosphate. Verify doses and G6PD considerations.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Oncology and nephrology immediately; PICU early; cardiology for significant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Hourly urine output, continuous rhythm observation, independent fluid/medication checks, and exact timing of repeat TLS labs.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at each lab interval; escalate for rising potassium/phosphate/creatinine, falling calcium with symptoms, arrhythmia, seizure, oliguria, or fluid overload.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; avoid fluid overload and prepare for escalation if pulmonary edema develops.

Medications/treatments: Uric-acid lowering therapy and electrolyte treatment per oncology/TLS pathway; treat hyperkalemia emergently; avoid routine calcium for asymptomatic hypocalcemia with high phosphate. Verify doses and G6PD considerations.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Venous thromboembolism
summary: Admit to monitored ward for confirmed symptomatic DVT/PE requiring anticoagulation; PICU for hemodynamic instability, significant hypoxemia, massive PE, intracranial thrombosis with deterioration or high bleeding risk.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward for confirmed symptomatic DVT/PE requiring anticoagulation; PICU for hemodynamic instability, significant hypoxemia, massive PE, intracranial thrombosis with deterioration or high bleeding risk.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; continuous monitoring for PE or unstable thrombosis.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bleeding checks, neurovascular/limb assessment, oxygenation and strict intake/output when renal disease affects anticoagulation.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and cardiopulmonary support for PE; avoid unnecessary ambulation in unstable PE but routine bed rest is not required for stable DVT.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for therapy/labs; avoid repeated traumatic procedures once anticoagulated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Regular diet; hydration appropriate to condition; NPO only if intervention planned.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/platelets, PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, renal/liver function, pregnancy test when applicable; anti-Xa or aPTT monitoring according to agent. Thrombophilia tests should be hematology-directed and timed appropriately.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Compression ultrasound for limb DVT; CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q imaging for PE based on stability/renal function; MRV/CTV for cerebral venous thrombosis.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start LMWH or unfractionated heparin using weight-based local anticoagulation protocol after bleeding-risk review. Thrombolysis/thrombectomy is reserved for selected life-/limb-threatening thrombosis with hematology/PICU/interventional team.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Hematology for all pediatric VTE; PICU/cardiology/interventional radiology/surgery for massive PE or threatened limb; remove provoking central line only with team plan.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Bleeding precautions, avoid IM injections/NSAIDs, dose/anti-Xa double checks, limb/neuro checks and anticoagulation education.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess symptoms and bleeding after each dose. New dyspnea/chest pain, hypotension, neurologic change, compartment signs or major bleeding requires immediate anticoagulation hold/reversal and PICU/hematology response.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and cardiopulmonary support for PE; avoid unnecessary ambulation in unstable PE but routine bed rest is not required for stable DVT.

Medications/treatments: Start LMWH or unfractionated heparin using weight-based local anticoagulation protocol after bleeding-risk review. Thrombolysis/thrombectomy is reserved for selected life-/limb-threatening thrombosis with hematology/PICU/interventional team.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Acute transfusion reaction
summary: Admit/transfer to monitored setting based on severity; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, hemolysis, anaphylaxis, TRALI, severe TACO or DIC.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit/transfer to monitored setting based on severity; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, hemolysis, anaphylaxis, TRALI, severe TACO or DIC.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Stop transfusion and obtain full vitals immediately; q5-15 min until stable, then q1-4h according to reaction.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/pulse oximetry for moderate-severe reaction; strict intake/output; monitor urine colour and fluid status.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support; manage anaphylaxis with IM epinephrine; ventilatory support for TRALI; upright position/diuresis for TACO when appropriate.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Keep line open with new tubing and 0.9% saline; do not restart the implicated product. Obtain additional access if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Treat shock with cautious isotonic boluses; avoid excess fluid in TACO. Regular diet when stable.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Notify blood bank immediately. Send post-reaction blood sample and implicated bag/tubing per protocol; CBC, DAT, bilirubin, LDH, haptoglobin, plasma/urine hemoglobin, renal tests, coagulation and cultures if septic reaction suspected.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for dyspnea/hypoxemia to assess edema/TRALI; other imaging source-directed.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treatment depends on phenotype—IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis, antipyretic for febrile nonhemolytic reaction after serious causes excluded, antibiotics for septic reaction, diuretic for TACO. Do not give antihistamine as a substitute for epinephrine.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Transfusion medicine/blood bank for every suspected reaction; hematology and PICU for severe reaction; ID for contaminated product/sepsis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Stop product, verify patient/unit identifiers, maintain IV with new saline tubing, preserve bag/tubing, document symptoms and exact times; complete reaction form.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess within minutes and trend hemolysis/renal/respiratory parameters. Worsening hypoxemia, hypotension, hemoglobinuria, oliguria or bleeding requires immediate PICU and reaction-specific treatment.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen and airway support; manage anaphylaxis with IM epinephrine; ventilatory support for TRALI; upright position/diuresis for TACO when appropriate.

Medications/treatments: Treatment depends on phenotype—IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis, antipyretic for febrile nonhemolytic reaction after serious causes excluded, antibiotics for septic reaction, diuretic for TACO. Do not give antihistamine as a substitute for epinephrine.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Breakthrough seizure in known epilepsy
summary: Admit to Ward if returned to baseline but observation/workup needed; PICU for ongoing seizures, respiratory support, severe encephalopathy or frequent rescue medication.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if returned to baseline but observation/workup needed; PICU for ongoing seizures, respiratory support, severe encephalopathy or frequent rescue medication.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Seizure precautions; continuous pulse oximetry/cardiorespiratory monitoring after rescue medication or ongoing events; neuro checks.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support during/post seizure; avoid routine oxygen if normal saturation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if repeated events, not baseline or medication load anticipated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral when safe; correct glucose/electrolytes/dehydration.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Point-of-care glucose; electrolytes/calcium/magnesium, antiseizure level and infection/toxicology tests only when indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging for typical breakthrough event with return to baseline; image for trauma, new focal deficit, persistent altered state, shunt concern or atypical presentation.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Continue home antiseizure medications on time; replace missed doses/load only with neurology/hospital pathway; rescue benzodiazepine per protocol; verify dose and maximum.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology for change from baseline, medication adjustment or recurrent events; PICU for status/airway.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Exact event timing/semiology, medication administration and recovery; ensure home medications are reconciled and available.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess immediately after seizure/rescue, then neuro checks q1–4 h depending on recovery.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support during/post seizure; avoid routine oxygen if normal saturation.
Medications/treatments: Continue home antiseizure medications on time; replace missed doses/load only with neurology/hospital pathway; rescue benzodiazepine per protocol; verify dose and maximum.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: First unprovoked seizure
summary: Admit to Ward if stable but observation/urgent testing needed; PICU for status, respiratory compromise or severe encephalopathy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if stable but observation/urgent testing needed; PICU for status, respiratory compromise or severe encephalopathy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Seizure precautions and neuro checks; continuous pulse ox after sedatives/rescue therapy.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if not baseline/prolonged/urgent tests.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Correct glucose/electrolyte abnormality; otherwise routine diet/fluids.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Point-of-care glucose; targeted electrolytes/calcium/magnesium, pregnancy test when relevant, toxicology or infection studies; routine broad labs are unnecessary in a well recovered child.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Emergent neuroimaging for persistent deficit, trauma, raised ICP, prolonged altered state or other red flags; outpatient MRI often preferred for stable focal seizure. ECG is important when syncope/arrhythmia possible.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Rescue benzodiazepine for prolonged recurrence. Long-term antiseizure medication is individualized with neurology, not automatic after every first seizure.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology; cardiology if syncope/abnormal ECG; child protection if injury/history concern.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Document semiology, duration and recovery; provide seizure first-aid teaching and water/heights safety.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess until baseline and after any recurrence; neuro checks q1–4 h based on concern.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.
Medications/treatments: Rescue benzodiazepine for prolonged recurrence. Long-term antiseizure medication is individualized with neurology, not automatic after every first seizure.

title: Febrile seizure
summary: Admit to Ward for stable complex/atypical event or infection needing admission; PICU for status, airway support or persistent encephalopathy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for stable complex/atypical event or infection needing admission; PICU for status, airway support or persistent encephalopathy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Seizure precautions and neuro checks; continuous pulse ox after rescue medication; fever and hydration monitoring.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if complex, not baseline or unable to drink.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral/IV as required.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose; targeted electrolytes/infection studies. LP is based on age, exam, immunization/antibiotic context and meningitis suspicion—not routine for a clear simple febrile seizure.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging for simple febrile seizure; image for focal deficit, trauma, raised ICP or persistent altered state.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat prolonged seizure per status pathway; antipyretics for comfort but they do not reliably prevent recurrence; no routine chronic antiseizure medication for simple febrile seizure.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/neurology for complex or atypical features; ID/PICU when CNS infection/status possible.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Document event and recovery; seizure first-aid teaching; monitor source of fever.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess until baseline; immediate review for recurrence; neuro checks q1–4 h if admitted.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

Medications/treatments: Treat prolonged seizure per status pathway; antipyretics for comfort but they do not reliably prevent recurrence; no routine chronic antiseizure medication for simple febrile seizure.

title: Status epilepticus
summary: Admit to PICU/step-down after convulsive status, repeated rescue medication, respiratory compromise, persistent altered mental status, or second-line antiseizure therapy; selected rapidly recovered patients may be managed on a monitored ward with neurology agreement.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU/step-down after convulsive status, repeated rescue medication, respiratory compromise, persistent altered mental status, or second-line antiseizure therapy; selected rapidly recovered patients may be managed on a monitored ward with neurology agreement.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during active seizure; q15 min after rescue until stable, then q1-2h. Record seizure start, medication times and measured weight/estimated weight.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG, pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring; bedside glucose immediately; frequent GCS/pupil/neuro checks; consider continuous EEG for persistent encephalopathy or suspected nonconvulsive status.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV/IO promptly, but do not delay first-line intranasal/buccal/IM benzodiazepine while obtaining access.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO until awake and swallow-safe; isotonic maintenance if needed. Correct hypoglycemia and clinically important electrolyte derangements promptly.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, electrolytes including calcium/magnesium, gas, CBC and antiseizure drug levels when relevant; toxicology, cultures/LP and metabolic studies based on cause. Pregnancy test when applicable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent CT for trauma, focal deficit, concern for hemorrhage/raised ICP or no recovery; MRI when stable for unexplained/focal status. Imaging must not delay seizure termination.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology and senior immediately; PICU/anesthesia for second-line therapy, respiratory depression, refractory seizure or persistent coma; ID for CNS infection concern; toxicology for ingestion.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Seizure precautions, oxygen/suction at bedside, no objects in mouth, document semiology and exact duration, independent medication double-check, monitor BP/respiration after each dose.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Assess at 5 min after each benzodiazepine and during second-line infusion. Ongoing seizure after adequate benzodiazepine plus second-line agent is refractory status—activate PICU/anesthesia and continuous-infusion pathway.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Position, suction, high-flow oxygen and bag-mask ventilation if needed; prepare for intubation after repeated benzodiazepines or refractory seizure, with PICU/anesthesia.

Medications/treatments: First line: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN/IM/buccal (max 10 mg; max 5 mg per nostril), repeat once after 5 min if required. If still seizing, give one second-line load: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1000 mg PE), or phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 1000 mg), per local algorithm.

guidance: CPS: Emergency management of convulsive status epilepticus.

title: Headache - secondary cause evaluation
summary: Admit to Ward for stable urgent evaluation; PICU for altered state, raised ICP, hypertensive emergency, CNS infection, hemorrhage or severe systemic illness.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for stable urgent evaluation; PICU for altered state, raised ICP, hypertensive emergency, CNS infection, hemorrhage or severe systemic illness.

sections.label: Respiratory support

sections.label: IV access

sections.label: Fluids / diet

sections.label: Labs

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency

title: Migraine
summary: Admit to Ward if neurologically stable and primary migraine likely; PICU only if alternate critical diagnosis or severe medication adverse effect.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if neurologically stable and primary migraine likely; PICU only if alternate critical diagnosis or severe medication adverse effect.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Routine vitals and neurologic reassessment; avoid unnecessary continuous monitoring unless sedating medications used.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: None.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if vomiting or IV therapy.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral hydration; isotonic bolus only for true deficit.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Usually none for established typical migraine with normal exam; targeted pregnancy/metabolic tests as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No imaging for typical recurrent migraine with normal exam; image if red flags or changed pattern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Use the current pediatric migraine pathway. Give early ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO (max 600 mg) or another age-appropriate analgesic when safe. For nausea/vomiting, ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/ODT (max 8 mg) is a reasonable first option. Metoclopramide or prochlorperazine may be pathway-specific alternatives but carry akathisia/dystonia risk; avoid or obtain expert review after a prior dystonic reaction. Review QT/electrolyte risk before combining QT-prolonging agents. Consider an age-appropriate triptan and specialist-directed therapy for refractory status. Avoid routine opioids. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology for atypical/refractory status or prevention plan; psychology/pain team for frequent disability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Dark quiet room, sleep, hydration, pain/nausea scoring; monitor extrapyramidal/QT effects when relevant.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess 30–60 minutes after each treatment step.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: None.

Medications/treatments: Use the current pediatric migraine pathway. Give early ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO (max 600 mg) or another age-appropriate analgesic when safe. For nausea/vomiting, ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/ODT (max 8 mg) is a reasonable first option. Review QT/electrolyte risk before combining QT-prolonging agents. Consider an age-appropriate triptan and specialist-directed therapy for refractory status. Avoid routine opioids. Verify doses.

title: Concussion
summary: Admit for persistent vomiting/severe headache, inability to ambulate or hydrate, prolonged symptoms, social/safeguarding concern, significant comorbidity or need for neuro observation; PICU/neurosurgery for deterioration or structural injury.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for persistent vomiting/severe headache, inability to ambulate or hydrate, prolonged symptoms, social/safeguarding concern, significant comorbidity or need for neuro observation; PICU/neurosurgery for deterioration or structural injury.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Neuro observations q2-4h while symptomatic; no routine continuous monitoring if otherwise stable.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support oxygen/ventilation; avoid hypoxia/hyperventilation except imminent herniation under expert direction.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if moderate/severe injury, vomiting or procedure.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Isotonic fluids; avoid hypotonic fluid and hypotension.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: None routinely.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Concussion is a clinical diagnosis; do not obtain CT routinely. Use PECARN/CPS head-trauma criteria for intracranial-injury risk.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Acetaminophen/ibuprofen when no contraindication, antiemetic as needed, sleep permitted with ordered neuro checks; avoid opioids/sedatives that obscure exam.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurosurgery only for imaging abnormality/deterioration; rehabilitation/concussion clinic for prolonged symptoms; child protection if mechanism is concerning.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Neuro observations at defined intervals; wake/sleep checks per local protocol; document vomiting and analgesia response.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Repeat neuro exam after analgesia/fluids and before discharge planning. Worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, focal deficit, seizure or declining GCS requires urgent CT/escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support oxygen/ventilation; avoid hypoxia/hyperventilation except imminent herniation under expert direction.
Medications/treatments: Acetaminophen/ibuprofen when no contraindication, antiemetic as needed, sleep permitted with ordered neuro checks; avoid opioids/sedatives that obscure exam.

title: Acute head injury / traumatic brain injury
summary: Admit to PICU/neurosurgery for intracranial injury, GCS <14, skull fracture with risk features, focal deficit, seizure, coagulopathy or deterioration; ward observation for selected stable injuries after senior review.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU/neurosurgery for intracranial injury, GCS <14, skull fracture with risk features, focal deficit, seizure, coagulopathy or deterioration; ward observation for selected stable injuries after senior review.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h with neuro observations initially; continuous monitoring for intracranial injury or altered mental status.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Serial GCS/pupils/vitals; continuous pulse ox after sedatives or severe injury; cervical-spine precautions when indicated.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support oxygen/ventilation; avoid hypoxia/hyperventilation except imminent herniation under expert direction.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if moderate/severe injury, vomiting or procedure.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Isotonic fluids; avoid hypotonic fluid and hypotension.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Targeted glucose/CBC/coagulation/type and screen for significant trauma; routine labs unnecessary for minor injury.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Apply CPS/PECARN criteria. Noncontrast head CT for high-risk features; cervical imaging according to mechanism/exam. Do not delay resuscitation or neurosurgical consultation.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Prevent hypoxia/hypotension, elevate head 30 degrees, keep neck midline, treat fever/pain/nausea, correct coagulopathy. Hypertonic saline for herniation/raised ICP only with PICU/neurosurgery pathway.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurosurgery/PICU for intracranial injury or decline; trauma/surgery for multisystem injury; child protection for inconsistent mechanism.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Neuro observations at defined intervals; wake/sleep checks per local protocol; document vomiting and analgesia response.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Any GCS drop >=2, new anisocoria/focal deficit, Cushing physiology, repeated vomiting or seizure is an emergency—call PICU/neurosurgery and repeat imaging/ICP management.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support oxygen/ventilation; avoid hypoxia/hyperventilation except imminent herniation under expert direction.

Medications/treatments: Prevent hypoxia/hypotension, elevate head 30 degrees, keep neck midline, treat fever/pain/nausea, correct coagulopathy. Hypertonic saline for herniation/raised ICP only with PICU/neurosurgery pathway.

title: Altered mental status / encephalopathy
summary: Admit to PICU/step-down when there is airway or ventilation risk, reduced GCS, recurrent severe agitation, a major metabolic abnormality, hemodynamic instability, or organ dysfunction; stable patients may be admitted to CTU/ward with frequent neurologic reassessment and a defined diagnostic plan.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU/step-down when there is airway or ventilation risk, reduced GCS, recurrent severe agitation, a major metabolic abnormality, hemodynamic instability, or organ dysfunction; stable patients may be admitted to CTU/ward with frequent neurologic reassessment and a defined diagnostic plan.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory/SpO₂; frequent GCS/pupils/glucose; strict I&O; temperature.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support early; intubation decision with PICU/anesthesia, recognizing cause-specific risks.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV/IO.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Treat shock/hypoglycemia/electrolytes; avoid hypotonic fluid.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, gas, electrolytes/calcium/magnesium, renal/liver tests, CBC, ammonia, toxicology and cultures based on context; pregnancy test when relevant; consider carboxyhemoglobin.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: CT/MRI/LP/EEG based on findings; do not delay treatment of hypoglycemia, sepsis, status or suspected cerebral injury.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Cause-directed antidote/antimicrobials/antiseizure therapy; minimize deliriogenic or obscuring sedatives.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: PICU early; neurology, toxicology/poison centre, ID, metabolic/endocrine, psychiatry or child protection as indicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Safe environment and 1:1 observation when necessary; serial neuro charting; retain medication containers/history.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Continuous when unstable; q15–60 min initially even if stable until trajectory understood.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support early; intubation decision with PICU/anesthesia, recognizing cause-specific risks.
Medications/treatments: Cause-directed antidote/antimicrobials/antiseizure therapy; minimize deliriogenic or obscuring sedatives.

title: VP shunt malfunction or infection
summary: Admit under neurosurgery/CTU only when stable with a defined plan; PICU for declining consciousness, recurrent apnea, hemodynamic instability, severe raised-ICP signs, or airway risk.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit under neurosurgery/CTU only when stable with a defined plan; PICU for declining consciousness, recurrent apnea, hemodynamic instability, severe raised-ICP signs, or airway risk.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; increase to continuous observation for any neurologic deterioration.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Serial GCS/age-appropriate mental status, pupils, fontanelle/head circumference in infants, vomiting, headache, eye movements, seizures, and shunt tract findings.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation; avoid hypoxia and hypotension. Position head midline/elevated if not contraindicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly; minimize sedation until neurosurgical assessment when raised ICP is possible.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO; isotonic IV fluids. Avoid hypotonic fluids and dehydration.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC/differential, CRP, electrolytes/glucose; blood cultures if febrile. CSF sampling only by neurosurgery or according to a defined shunt-infection pathway.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Rapid MRI or CT brain and shunt-series imaging according to local neurosurgical pathway and prior baseline; do not delay neurosurgery for imaging in a deteriorating child.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Analgesia/antiemetic without oversedation; seizure treatment as required; antibiotics only after cultures when stable, but immediately if septic. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurosurgery urgently for all suspected malfunctions/infections; PICU for deterioration; ID for shunt infection.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Frequent neuro checks, NPO, seizure precautions, document shunt reservoir/tract changes without manipulating the shunt, and record vomiting/headache trend.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at least hourly until the plan is established; call neurosurgery/PICU immediately for GCS decline, bradycardia with hypertension, unequal pupils, new seizure, apnea, or progressive vomiting/headache.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation; avoid hypoxia and hypotension. Position head midline/elevated if not contraindicated.
Medications/treatments: Analgesia/antiemetic without oversedation; seizure treatment as required; antibiotics only after cultures when stable, but immediately if septic. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Acute weakness / ataxia / possible Guillain-Barre syndrome
summary: Admit to neurology/CTU for objective weakness, gait loss, bulbar symptoms, areflexia, autonomic symptoms, or uncertain trajectory; PICU for respiratory weakness, bulbar dysfunction, rapid progression, significant dysautonomia, or inability to protect airway.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to neurology/CTU for objective weakness, gait loss, bulbar symptoms, areflexia, autonomic symptoms, or uncertain trajectory; PICU for respiratory weakness, bulbar dysfunction, rapid progression, significant dysautonomia, or inability to protect airway.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h if stable; q1-2h with progression or autonomic instability.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Serial neurologic examination, reflexes, cranial nerves, gait, swallowing, pain, bladder function; cardiorespiratory monitoring for suspected GBS/dysautonomia.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Measure forced vital capacity/negative inspiratory force or local age-appropriate respiratory metrics serially; involve RT early. Do not wait for hypoxemia to recognize ventilatory failure.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if progressive symptoms, planned IVIG, poor intake, or diagnostic procedures are likely.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Swallow screen before oral intake when bulbar symptoms exist; isotonic IV fluids if NPO. Monitor constipation/urinary retention.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, electrolytes including magnesium/phosphate, CBC, CK, inflammatory/infectious/toxic studies as indicated; lumbar puncture only after neurologic review and when safe.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: MRI brain/spine for focal findings, cord/brainstem concern, or alternative diagnosis; not every classic GBS presentation requires emergent imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat the underlying diagnosis; IVIG or plasma exchange for GBS per neurology; pain control and VTE/pressure-injury prevention as appropriate. Avoid sedating respiratory depressants.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neurology urgently; PICU/RT for respiratory or bulbar signs; physio/OT/SLP; toxicology if exposure concern.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Falls precautions, assisted transfers, aspiration precautions, bladder/bowel monitoring, frequent strength checks, and prompt reporting of autonomic swings.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess neurologic and respiratory function at least q2-4h and more often if changing; escalate for declining respiratory metrics, weak cough, pooling secretions, facial/bulbar weakness, rapidly ascending weakness, or arrhythmia/BP instability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Measure forced vital capacity/negative inspiratory force or local age-appropriate respiratory metrics serially; involve RT early. Do not wait for hypoxemia to recognize ventilatory failure.

Medications/treatments: Treat the underlying diagnosis; IVIG or plasma exchange for GBS per neurology; pain control and VTE/pressure-injury prevention as appropriate. Avoid sedating respiratory depressants.

title: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration
summary: Admit to Ward for stable rehydration; PICU for shock, severe sodium disturbance, altered state or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for stable rehydration; PICU for shock, severe sodium disturbance, altered state or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, hydration checks, strict I&O and stool/emesis record; daily weight; cardiorespiratory monitoring if severe electrolyte disturbance.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support only as indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV/NG if oral rehydration fails or shock.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral/NG rehydration preferred. For shock, isotonic bolus <mL/kg> with reassessment; replace deficit/losses carefully, especially dysnatremia.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose and electrolytes/renal function for moderate-severe dehydration, IV fluids, altered state or prolonged losses; stool testing only for selected bloody, severe, outbreak, travel or immunocompromised cases.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging; obtain for focal peritonism, obstruction, intussusception or alternate diagnosis.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: For age ≥6 months with vomiting that prevents oral rehydration, consider ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/ODT once (max 8 mg; 8–15 kg: 2 mg, 15–30 kg: 4 mg, >30 kg: 6–8 mg), then restart oral rehydration 15–30 minutes later. Do not routinely schedule multidose ondansetron or substitute dimenhydrinate, metoclopramide, domperidone or phenothiazines for uncomplicated gastroenteritis. Ondansetron may increase diarrhea; it is less useful when moderate-severe diarrhea predominates. Review QT risk/electrolytes when congenital long-QT, significant hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, repeated/IV doses or other QT-prolonging drugs are present. No routine antidiarrheals or antibiotics except specific indications. Verify all doses locally.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/PICU for shock/dysnatremia; surgery for peritonism/bilious emesis; ID/public health for selected pathogen/outbreak.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Measured oral challenge, wet diapers/urine, replace ongoing losses per order; infection-control hygiene.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess after each bolus and within 1–2 hours of oral/NG trial; repeat sodium at a rate appropriate to abnormality.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support only as indicated.

Medications/treatments: For age ≥6 months with vomiting that prevents oral rehydration, consider ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/ODT once (max 8 mg; 8–15 kg: 2 mg, 15–30 kg: 4 mg, >30 kg: 6–8 mg), then restart oral rehydration 15–30 minutes later. Do not routinely schedule multidose ondansetron or substitute dimenhydrinate, metoclopramide, domperidone or phenothiazines for uncomplicated gastroenteritis. Ondansetron may increase diarrhea; it is less useful when moderate-severe diarrhea predominates. Review QT risk/electrolytes when congenital long-QT, significant hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, repeated/IV doses or other QT-prolonging drugs are present. No routine antidiarrheals or antibiotics except specific indications. Verify all doses locally.

title: Undifferentiated abdominal pain
summary: Admit to Ward for serial exams when stable; surgery/PICU for peritonitis, obstruction, hemorrhage, shock or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for serial exams when stable; surgery/PICU for peritonitis, obstruction, hemorrhage, shock or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, serial pain and abdominal exams; strict I&O; cardiorespiratory monitoring if unstable/opioids.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if NPO, vomiting or ill.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: NPO with isotonic maintenance; bolus only for hypoperfusion.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Targeted CBC, electrolytes/renal/liver tests, lipase, CRP, urinalysis/culture, glucose/ketones, pregnancy test and STI testing as appropriate.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Ultrasound first for many pediatric abdominal/gynecologic questions; radiograph for obstruction/foreign body; CT/MRI after senior/surgical discussion.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat pain promptly and select antiemetic therapy only after reviewing surgical, pregnancy, metabolic, intracranial and toxic causes. Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg) is a common first option. Dimenhydrinate may be considered for selected nonspecific/vestibular nausea when sedation is acceptable. Avoid routine dopamine antagonists after prior dystonia and avoid stacking QT-prolonging agents without ECG, potassium and magnesium review. Antiemetics must not delay imaging, surgical review or source control. Antibiotics only for suspected infection after cultures/source plan.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Surgery early for peritonism/obstruction; gynecology/urology for torsion; GI/endocrine/toxicology based on cause.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: NPO status, timed serial exams, emesis/stool/urine, pain response; chaperone and consent for sensitive exams.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Re-examine within 1–2 hours and after analgesia; immediately for worsening vitals/pain.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

Medications/treatments: Treat pain promptly and select antiemetic therapy only after reviewing surgical, pregnancy, metabolic, intracranial and toxic causes. Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg) is a common first option. Dimenhydrinate may be considered for selected nonspecific/vestibular nausea when sedation is acceptable. Avoid routine dopamine antagonists after prior dystonia and avoid stacking QT-prolonging agents without ECG, potassium and magnesium review. Antiemetics must not delay imaging, surgical review or source control. Antibiotics only for suspected infection after cultures/source plan.

title: Suspected appendicitis
summary: Admit under or jointly with pediatric surgery according to the local model; use PICU for septic shock, severe perforated disease, or organ dysfunction.

sections.text: Admit under or jointly with pediatric surgery according to the local model; use PICU for septic shock, severe perforated disease, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, pain and serial abdominal exam; strict I&O.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as indicated.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: NPO with isotonic fluid; bolus if hypoperfused.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP, electrolytes/renal function, urinalysis, pregnancy test when relevant; blood culture if septic.

sections.label: Medications / treatment

sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: NPO, timed antibiotics, pain scores, serial exam and urine output.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Surgical reassessment after imaging and within hours; immediate review for worsening peritonitis/instability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as indicated.

title: Constipation or fecal impaction
summary: Admit to Ward for supervised disimpaction if stable; surgery for obstruction/perforation concern.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for supervised disimpaction if stable; surgery for obstruction/perforation concern.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Routine vitals, intake/output and stool record; abdominal reassessment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: None.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV only if dehydrated or unable to tolerate enteral regimen.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral/NG fluids; avoid excess maintenance.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Usually none; electrolytes/thyroid/celiac/calcium only for red flags or refractory course.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine abdominal radiograph; image for obstruction/foreign body or diagnostic uncertainty.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Oral/NG polyethylene glycol-based cleanout per local protocol; enemas only when indicated and age-appropriate; avoid phosphate enemas in high-risk children. Maintenance plan must follow disimpaction.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI for refractory/red flags; surgery for obstruction; child life/psychology as needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Document stool quantity/consistency, pain and emesis; privacy and skin care.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess every few hours during cleanout; stop and review for worsening pain/distension/vomiting.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: None.

Medications/treatments: Oral/NG polyethylene glycol-based cleanout per local protocol; enemas only when indicated and age-appropriate; avoid phosphate enemas in high-risk children. Maintenance plan must follow disimpaction.

title: Bowel obstruction / bilious vomiting
summary: Admit under pediatric surgery; any neonate/child with true bilious emesis, peritonitis, shock, severe distension or suspected volvulus requires immediate surgical escalation and PICU consideration.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit under pediatric surgery; any neonate/child with true bilious emesis, peritonitis, shock, severe distension or suspected volvulus requires immediate surgical escalation and PICU consideration.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until diagnosis/stable; continuous monitoring if ill or after resuscitation.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict intake/output, urine output, abdominal girth/exam and NG losses; serial perfusion and pain assessment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if unstable; aspiration precautions and suction available.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two IVs if unstable or likely operation; obtain type and screen.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO. Isotonic crystalloid bolus 10-20 mL/kg for dehydration/shock with reassessment; replace ongoing NG losses with appropriate isotonic fluid/electrolytes; maintenance with dextrose based on age.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, electrolytes, glucose, gas/lactate, renal/liver tests, lipase as indicated, coagulation and type/screen; blood culture if septic.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Abdominal radiographs and urgent upper-GI contrast study/ultrasound according to age and concern for malrotation/volvulus; do not delay surgery for unstable/peritonitic child.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: NPO, urgent NG/OG decompression, analgesia and surgical management are primary. A single antiemetic such as ondansetron may be used as an adjunct after ECG/electrolyte review when appropriate, but must not delay decompression, contrast imaging or surgery and must not create false reassurance. Avoid prokinetics when mechanical obstruction is possible. Give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics for suspected ischemia, perforation, peritonitis or sepsis.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Pediatric surgery immediately; radiology for time-critical study; PICU/anesthesia for instability/operation.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: NPO, NG to ordered suction, measure/replace losses, serial abdomen and perfusion, prepare for OR and maintain thermal control in neonates.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess after decompression/fluids and at least hourly if concerning. Increasing pain, tenderness, distension, bloody stool, rising lactate, fever or shock suggests ischemia/perforation and mandates immediate operation pathway.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if unstable; aspiration precautions and suction available.

Medications/treatments: NPO, urgent NG/OG decompression, analgesia and surgical management are primary. A single antiemetic such as ondansetron may be used as an adjunct after ECG/electrolyte review when appropriate, but must not delay decompression, contrast imaging or surgery and must not create false reassurance. Avoid prokinetics when mechanical obstruction is possible. Give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics for suspected ischemia, perforation, peritonitis or sepsis.

title: Intussusception
summary: Admit under pediatrics/surgery after reduction according to local pathway; immediate surgical/PICU care for shock, perforation, peritonitis, failed reduction or bowel ischemia.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit under pediatrics/surgery after reduction according to local pathway; immediate surgical/PICU care for shock, perforation, peritonitis, failed reduction or bowel ischemia.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until reduced/stable, then q4h; frequent pain and abdominal assessments.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Pulse oximetry during sedation/reduction; strict intake/output; observe for recurrent episodic pain, vomiting or bloody stool.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; procedural sedation support as required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain IV before reduction, especially with dehydration, significant pain, vomiting or possible surgery.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO before reduction. Give isotonic bolus 10-20 mL/kg for dehydration/shock with reassessment; after successful uncomplicated reduction, advance feeds per surgery/radiology pathway.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, electrolytes, glucose and type/screen if ill, prolonged symptoms, bleeding, dehydration or surgery possible; no routine labs in a very well child if local pathway allows.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent abdominal ultrasound. Proceed to air/contrast enema for diagnosis and reduction when no perforation/peritonitis and expertise is available; abdominal radiograph for obstruction/perforation concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Analgesia and antiemetic; do not delay reduction. Give antibiotics if perforation, peritonitis, sepsis or operative management is suspected.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Pediatric surgery and radiology early; PICU/anesthesia for instability, perforation or high-risk sedation.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: NPO, serial abdomen/pain chart, document stool/emesis and time of reduction, monitor closely after reduction for recurrence.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess immediately after reduction and serially for at least the local observation period. Recurrent colicky pain/vomiting, peritonism, fever or instability requires repeat ultrasound and urgent surgery review.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; procedural sedation support as required.
Medications/treatments: Analgesia and antiemetic; do not delay reduction. Give antibiotics if perforation, peritonitis, sepsis or operative management is suspected.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Gastrointestinal bleeding
summary: Admit to GI/CTU for ongoing or significant hematemesis, melena/hematochezia with anemia or instability, recurrent bleeding, high-risk comorbidity, or need for endoscopy; PICU for shock, major transfusion, airway risk, or severe ongoing hemorrhage.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to GI/CTU for ongoing or significant hematemesis, melena/hematochezia with anemia or instability, recurrent bleeding, high-risk comorbidity, or need for endoscopy; PICU for shock, major transfusion, airway risk, or severe ongoing hemorrhage.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h during active bleeding or instability; q4h only after clear stabilization.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring if significant bleed; strict I&O; quantify emesis/stool, perfusion, mental status, and orthostatic symptoms when appropriate.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Protect airway with massive hematemesis or altered mental status; oxygen as needed; early anesthesia/PICU involvement for airway risk.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two large-bore IVs for significant bleeding; type and cross promptly.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO; cautious isotonic resuscitation and blood products according to hemodynamics/labs; avoid excessive crystalloid dilution.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC serially, type and screen/cross, coagulation/fibrinogen, electrolytes/urea/creatinine, liver profile; stool/infectious studies and pregnancy testing when relevant.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Usually endoscopy-directed; ultrasound/CT/Meckel scan or other imaging based on age and suspected source after specialist review.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Acid suppression for suspected upper GI source per pathway; octreotide or other targeted therapy only with GI/PICU; correct coagulopathy and stop offending drugs. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI urgently for significant/ongoing bleed; surgery/interventional radiology for uncontrolled bleeding; PICU/transfusion medicine for instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Save/photograph samples when appropriate, quantify blood loss, maintain NPO, monitor IV access, and document transfusion response/reaction.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after each resuscitative step and repeat CBC based on bleeding rate; escalate for tachycardia with poor perfusion, falling hemoglobin, recurrent large-volume bleeding, syncope, altered mental status, or increasing transfusion need.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Protect airway with massive hematemesis or altered mental status; oxygen as needed; early anesthesia/PICU involvement for airway risk.

Medications/treatments: Acid suppression for suspected upper GI source per pathway; octreotide or other targeted therapy only with GI/PICU; correct coagulopathy and stop offending drugs. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Acute pancreatitis
summary: Admit to GI/CTU for pain requiring IV therapy, vomiting/dehydration, inability to tolerate enteral intake, organ dysfunction, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, severe electrolyte disturbance, or multiorgan dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to GI/CTU for pain requiring IV therapy, vomiting/dehydration, inability to tolerate enteral intake, organ dysfunction, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for shock, respiratory failure, severe electrolyte disturbance, or multiorgan dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h when severe or after opioid escalation.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, pain/nausea scores, daily weight, respiratory status, abdominal examination; continuous pulse oximetry with significant opioids or respiratory compromise.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; assess for pleural effusion/ARDS in severe disease.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second line if severe, frequent labs, or substantial fluid/analgesia needs.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Early isotonic IV resuscitation when depleted with frequent reassessment; begin early enteral nutrition as tolerated rather than prolonged bowel rest; avoid fluid overload.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Lipase, CBC, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, glucose, calcium, triglycerides; repeat only to monitor organ dysfunction rather than chase lipase. Cause-directed tests.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Ultrasound for biliary disease; CT/MRI only for diagnostic uncertainty, complications, or failure to improve, usually after specialist review.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Multimodal analgesia and a stepwise antiemetic plan. Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg) is a common first option. If nausea persists, reassess hydration, ileus, electrolyte abnormalities and complications before adding another agent; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Avoid dopamine antagonists after prior dystonia and review QT/electrolyte risk before combination therapy. No routine antibiotics unless infected necrosis, cholangitis or another bacterial source; treat the cause. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI; surgery for gallstone/structural disease; PICU for severe disease; pain team if difficult control.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Pain and sedation monitoring, strict fluid balance, early feeding tolerance, glucose checks when abnormal, and respiratory observation with opioids.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess pain, perfusion, urine output, and respiratory status within 1-2h after treatment; escalate for shock, oliguria, hypoxemia, increasing abdominal distension, GI bleed, or worsening organ dysfunction.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; assess for pleural effusion/ARDS in severe disease.

Medications/treatments: Multimodal analgesia and a stepwise antiemetic plan. Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg) is a common first option. If nausea persists, reassess hydration, ileus, electrolyte abnormalities and complications before adding another agent; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Avoid dopamine antagonists after prior dystonia and review QT/electrolyte risk before combination therapy. No routine antibiotics unless infected necrosis, cholangitis or another bacterial source; treat the cause. Verify doses.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease flare
summary: Admit to GI/CTU for moderate-severe flare, frequent bloody stools, significant anemia, dehydration, weight loss/malnutrition, severe pain, inability to tolerate oral therapy, or toxic megacolon concern; PICU for shock, perforation, severe hemorrhage, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to GI/CTU for moderate-severe flare, frequent bloody stools, significant anemia, dehydration, weight loss/malnutrition, severe pain, inability to tolerate oral therapy, or toxic megacolon concern; PICU for shock, perforation, severe hemorrhage, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h when systemically unwell or significant bleeding is present.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, stool count/blood, abdominal girth/exam, pain, fever, daily weight, nutritional intake; VTE risk assessment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: As needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for moderate-severe flare, IV medications, dehydration, or significant anemia.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Isotonic rehydration; enteral nutrition as tolerated with dietitian/GI guidance; NPO only for obstruction, severe ileus, perforation concern, or procedure.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, CRP/ESR, electrolytes/renal/liver profile, albumin, iron studies as appropriate; stool culture/C. difficile and other infectious testing before escalating immunosuppression.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Abdominal radiograph for severe colitis/distension or toxic megacolon concern; ultrasound/MR/CT for complications according to GI/surgery.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Continue/adjust IBD therapy with GI; corticosteroids/biologic rescue per pathway after infection assessment; analgesia avoiding NSAIDs and minimizing opioids; VTE prophylaxis when indicated. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI early; surgery for toxic megacolon, perforation, obstruction, abscess, or refractory severe colitis; dietitian; hematology for VTE/major anemia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Accurate stool chart, abdominal girth when indicated, nutrition intake, bleeding, VTE prevention, and prompt reporting of distension or reduced bowel sounds.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess at least q4h and review daily severity score if used; escalate for tachycardia, fever, worsening distension/tenderness, reduced bowel sounds, peritonitis, falling hemoglobin, or systemic toxicity.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: As needed.

Medications/treatments: Continue/adjust IBD therapy with GI; corticosteroids/biologic rescue per pathway after infection assessment; analgesia avoiding NSAIDs and minimizing opioids; VTE prophylaxis when indicated. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Feeding intolerance / vomiting in a medically complex child
summary: Admit to CTU/complex care for dehydration, recurrent emesis with aspiration risk, feed intolerance preventing medication/nutrition delivery, device complication, respiratory compromise, or caregiver concern for deviation from baseline; PICU for airway/ventilatory failure, shock, or severe neurologic change.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to CTU/complex care for dehydration, recurrent emesis with aspiration risk, feed intolerance preventing medication/nutrition delivery, device complication, respiratory compromise, or caregiver concern for deviation from baseline; PICU for airway/ventilatory failure, shock, or severe neurologic change.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if near baseline; q1-2h during respiratory, neurologic, or perfusion concern.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Compare with documented baseline; strict I&O, emesis/stool, abdominal exam, respiratory secretion burden, device function, and seizure/mental-status trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Continue verified home support and airway-clearance plan; involve RT early for oxygen/NIV/tracheostomy/cough-assist needs; use only equipment settings confirmed with family/chart.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain if dehydrated, unable to give essential medications, significant labs are required, or deterioration is possible.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Hold or reduce feeds initially when aspiration/obstruction is possible; provide isotonic IV hydration; restart home formula/route gradually after the cause and safety plan are clear.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Targeted glucose, electrolytes, renal function, gas, CBC/cultures, drug levels, or urinalysis based on presentation; avoid broad testing without a clinical question.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Confirm tube position or obtain abdominal/chest imaging only when device displacement, obstruction, aspiration, constipation, or another complication is suspected.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: First identify and treat device displacement, obstruction, constipation, infection, aspiration, dysmotility, pain or medication toxicity. Reconcile all home medications and time-critical drugs. Do not automatically suppress vomiting before excluding bilious obstruction, aspiration risk or tube malfunction. When an antiemetic is appropriate, ondansetron is a common first option; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Prokinetics such as metoclopramide or domperidone require a defined dysmotility indication and local GI/pharmacy guidance. Avoid unverified substitutions and review QT/EPS risk.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Complex care/primary subspecialty, dietitian, GI/surgery/IR for tube issues, SLP for aspiration concern, palliative care when already involved; PICU early if baseline support is exceeded.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Document baseline versus current status, home-device settings/sizes, emergency trach/G-tube supplies, feed/med schedule, caregiver expertise, and individualized escalation plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after hydration, suction/airway clearance, and any feed trial; escalate for support above baseline, recurrent aspiration, bilious emesis, device dislodgement with tract concern, prolonged seizure, or caregiver report that the child is significantly unlike baseline.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Continue verified home support and airway-clearance plan; involve RT early for oxygen/NIV/tracheostomy/cough-assist needs; use only equipment settings confirmed with family/chart.

Medications/treatments: First identify and treat device displacement, obstruction, constipation, infection, aspiration, dysmotility, pain or medication toxicity. Reconcile all home medications and time-critical drugs. Do not automatically suppress vomiting before excluding bilious obstruction, aspiration risk or tube malfunction. When an antiemetic is appropriate, ondansetron is a common first option; dimenhydrinate may be considered when sedation is acceptable. Prokinetics such as metoclopramide or domperidone require a defined dysmotility indication and local GI/pharmacy guidance. Avoid unverified substitutions and review QT/EPS risk.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Acute kidney injury (AKI)
summary: Admit to Ward if stable with close monitoring; PICU/nephrology urgently for hyperkalemia, severe acidosis, pulmonary edema, uremic symptoms, shock or dialysis consideration.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward if stable with close monitoring; PICU/nephrology urgently for hyperkalemia, severe acidosis, pulmonary edema, uremic symptoms, shock or dialysis consideration.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict hourly/shift urine output, daily weight, BP and cumulative fluid balance; cardiac monitoring for potassium abnormality.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/ventilation for pulmonary edema; avoid fluid overload.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access; urinary catheter only if necessary for accurate output/retention assessment.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: If hypovolemic, cautious isotonic challenge with reassessment; if euvolemic/overloaded, stop routine fluids and individualize.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Serial electrolytes/urea/creatinine/glucose/bicarbonate, calcium/phosphate/magnesium; urinalysis/microscopy, urine protein/creatinine; CK for rhabdo; hemolysis/complement/autoimmune tests as indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Renal/bladder ultrasound for obstruction or unclear AKI; source-directed imaging.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop nephrotoxins and renally adjust all medications; treat hyperkalemia/acidosis/pulmonary edema per emergency pathway; avoid NSAIDs. Diuretics do not cure AKI but may help overload under expert plan.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology early for stage 2–3, unclear intrinsic disease, significant electrolyte/overload or no improvement; PICU for dialysis-level indications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Daily weight same scale, strict inputs/outputs, avoid potassium-containing fluids unless reviewed, pharmacy renal dosing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess after any fluid intervention; labs q2–12 h depending on severity; immediate response to ECG/urine changes.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/ventilation for pulmonary edema; avoid fluid overload.

Medications/treatments: Stop nephrotoxins and renally adjust all medications; treat hyperkalemia/acidosis/pulmonary edema per emergency pathway; avoid NSAIDs. Diuretics do not cure AKI but may help overload under expert plan.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.
