title: Nephrotic syndrome
summary: Admit to Ward for stable edema/workup; PICU for shock, pulmonary edema, major thrombosis or severe infection.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for stable edema/workup; PICU for shock, pulmonary edema, major thrombosis or severe infection.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Daily weight, strict I&O, BP, edema/abdominal girth; monitor perfusion and respiratory status.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen for pulmonary edema/effusion; escalate support.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if complicated or albumin/IV therapy planned.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Avoid routine bolus for edema. Albumin/diuretic therapy only for selected severe edema or symptomatic hypovolemia with nephrology/local protocol and close monitoring.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Urinalysis, urine protein/creatinine, serum albumin, electrolytes/creatinine, CBC; complement/other tests for atypical features; cultures if febrile.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Ultrasound/Doppler for thrombosis or renal imaging when atypical; CXR for respiratory symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Steroid regimen for typical first episode/relapse per nephrology/local protocol; infection treatment; anticoagulation only for confirmed/high-risk indication with specialist. Avoid NSAIDs.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology for first/complicated/atypical cases; ID/surgery for peritonitis; hematology for thrombosis.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Daily urine protein if pathway, weights, BP, edema and abdominal pain; thrombosis precautions/ambulation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess volume status after any albumin/diuretic and at least q4 h when complicated.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen for pulmonary edema/effusion; escalate support.

Medications/treatments: Steroid regimen for typical first episode/relapse per nephrology/local protocol; infection treatment; anticoagulation only for confirmed/high-risk indication with specialist. Avoid NSAIDs.

title: Nephritic syndrome / glomerulonephritis
summary: Admit to nephrology/CTU for hypertension, AKI, oliguria, edema, gross hematuria with systemic features, electrolyte abnormality, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for hypertensive emergency, pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, or rapidly progressive renal failure.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to nephrology/CTU for hypertension, AKI, oliguria, edema, gross hematuria with systemic features, electrolyte abnormality, or uncertain diagnosis; PICU for hypertensive emergency, pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, or rapidly progressive renal failure.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: BP with correct cuff q2-4h; more frequently if severe hypertension or symptoms.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, edema, respiratory status, neurologic symptoms, and fluid balance; continuous monitoring for severe hypertension/electrolyte disturbance.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema; elevate head and involve PICU/nephrology early.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for significant hypertension, AKI, IV therapy, or frequent labs.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Sodium/fluid restriction according to volume status; avoid nephrotoxins and potassium excess; do not give routine maintenance fluid to an oliguric, fluid-overloaded child.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Urinalysis/microscopy, urine protein/creatinine, CBC, electrolytes/urea/creatinine, albumin, complement, streptococcal studies and autoimmune/infectious tests as directed; ECG for hyperkalemia.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Renal ultrasound for atypical course, significant AKI, obstruction concern, or nephrology recommendation; chest imaging for pulmonary edema.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat hypertension and fluid overload per nephrology/hospital pathway; diuretic only when appropriate; antibiotics only for active infection, not solely positive serology. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology early; PICU for emergency features; rheumatology for systemic autoimmune concern.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Accurate BP technique, strict fluid/sodium plan, daily weight, urine output/appearance, edema and respiratory observations.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess BP, urine output, electrolytes, and respiratory status at defined intervals; escalate for severe headache/visual symptoms, seizure, pulmonary edema, hyperkalemia, anuria, or rapidly rising creatinine.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema; elevate head and involve PICU/nephrology early.

Medications/treatments: Treat hypertension and fluid overload per nephrology/hospital pathway; diuretic only when appropriate; antibiotics only for active infection, not solely positive serology. Verify doses.

title: Hypertension / hypertensive emergency
summary: Admit to PICU for hypertensive emergency/encephalopathy, severe symptoms or IV antihypertensive infusion; ward for stable urgency with specialist plan.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to PICU for hypertensive emergency/encephalopathy, severe symptoms or IV antihypertensive infusion; ward for stable urgency with specialist plan.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Repeat manual BP with correct cuff; frequent four-limb/serial BP as appropriate; cardiorespiratory and neuro monitoring in severe cases; strict I&O.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema or neuro compromise.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access for severe/symptomatic cases.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Avoid unnecessary bolus; manage volume based on cause.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Electrolytes/creatinine, urinalysis/protein, CBC, glucose; pregnancy/toxicology/endocrine tests as indicated; ECG/troponin/BNP if cardiac symptoms.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Renal ultrasound/Doppler, echocardiogram, neuroimaging and other tests based on urgency/organ injury.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Hypertensive emergency requires controlled, gradual BP reduction with titratable IV agent per PICU/nephrology; avoid abrupt normalization. Stable urgency uses oral therapy under specialist plan.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology/PICU urgently; cardiology, neurology, toxicology or endocrinology by cause.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: BP technique/cuff documented; neuro/vision/chest symptoms and urine output; avoid PRN treatment without clear thresholds and senior plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Every 5–15 minutes during IV titration; q30–60 min in severe urgency initially; trend against planned reduction target.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema or neuro compromise.

Medications/treatments: Hypertensive emergency requires controlled, gradual BP reduction with titratable IV agent per PICU/nephrology; avoid abrupt normalization. Stable urgency uses oral therapy under specialist plan.

title: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
summary: Admit to nephrology/CTU; PICU for neurologic symptoms, severe hypertension, pulmonary edema, significant bleeding, hyperkalemia, anuria, shock, or dialysis-level indications.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to nephrology/CTU; PICU for neurologic symptoms, severe hypertension, pulmonary edema, significant bleeding, hyperkalemia, anuria, shock, or dialysis-level indications.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h with frequent BP; q1h if unstable or severe hypertension.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict I&O, daily weight, fluid balance, neurologic checks, bleeding, perfusion; cardiorespiratory monitoring for severe electrolyte/BP abnormalities.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema or encephalopathy-related airway compromise.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; avoid unnecessary central access until nephrology plan unless emergent dialysis is required.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Carefully match fluids to volume status and urine output; avoid overload, nephrotoxins, and potassium load. Early isotonic volume expansion may be considered only before established oliguria and with specialist guidance.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Serial CBC/platelets, smear, reticulocytes, LDH/bilirubin/haptoglobin, electrolytes/urea/creatinine, glucose, urinalysis; stool testing for Shiga toxin when diarrheal illness is present; coagulation to assess alternatives.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Renal ultrasound or neuroimaging only when indicated; chest radiograph for pulmonary edema.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Supportive care; transfuse RBCs for clinically significant anemia with nephrology guidance; avoid routine platelet transfusion unless major bleeding/procedure; treat hypertension/electrolytes and arrange dialysis when indicated. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology immediately; hematology for atypical/TMA uncertainty; PICU for severe disease; ID/public health as locally required for enteric pathogen.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Contact precautions for diarrheal illness per policy, strict fluid balance, frequent BP, bleeding/neuro checks, and avoidance of NSAIDs/nephrotoxins.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess labs, BP, urine output, and neurologic status at least q4-6h in evolving disease; escalate for anuria, hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, seizure, severe headache, worsening thrombocytopenia/anemia, or altered mental status.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support for pulmonary edema or encephalopathy-related airway compromise.

Medications/treatments: Supportive care; transfuse RBCs for clinically significant anemia with nephrology guidance; avoid routine platelet transfusion unless major bleeding/procedure; treat hypertension/electrolytes and arrange dialysis when indicated. Verify doses.

title: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
summary: Admit to monitored ward/step-down after terminated SVT if first episode, infant, medication initiation, prolonged event or uncertain recurrence risk; PICU for shock, persistent SVT, ventricular dysfunction or infusion therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward/step-down after terminated SVT if first episode, infant, medication initiation, prolonged event or uncertain recurrence risk; PICU for shock, persistent SVT, ventricular dysfunction or infusion therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during tachycardia; q15 min after conversion until stable, then q2-4h.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous ECG/telemetry and pulse oximetry; obtain rhythm strip/12-lead ECG before and after conversion whenever this does not delay treatment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if hypoxemic or poorly perfused; prepare for sedation/airway support if cardioversion is required.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain IV/IO promptly; use the most proximal line possible for adenosine with immediate saline flush.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during active unstable rhythm; cautious isotonic fluid only if preload depletion is likely because cardiomyopathy may coexist.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, electrolytes including potassium/magnesium/calcium, CBC and thyroid tests if indicated; troponin/BNP and gas/lactate when prolonged or unstable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph/echocardiogram when heart failure, structural disease, prolonged tachycardia or abnormal exam is present.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stable narrow-complex regular SVT: vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV push (max 6 mg) followed by flush; if unsuccessful, 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg). Unstable SVT: synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if needed. Further antiarrhythmic therapy is cardiology/PICU-directed.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology for first/recurrent SVT and maintenance plan; PICU immediately for instability, refractory rhythm or ventricular dysfunction; anesthesia if cardioversion sedation is needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Save rhythm strips, apply defibrillation pads early if unstable, record exact rates/medication times, teach family pulse/recurrence plan when appropriate.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Confirm sustained sinus rhythm and perfusion after each intervention. Recurrent SVT, hypotension, altered mental status, chest pain, pulmonary edema or poor perfusion requires immediate synchronized cardioversion/PICU.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen if hypoxemic or poorly perfused; prepare for sedation/airway support if cardioversion is required.

Medications/treatments: Stable narrow-complex regular SVT: vagal manoeuvres, then adenosine 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV push (max 6 mg) followed by flush; if unsuccessful, 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg). Unstable SVT: synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg if needed. Further antiarrhythmic therapy is cardiology/PICU-directed.

title: Syncope
summary: Admit to monitored ward for exertional/supine syncope, abnormal ECG, known heart disease, family history of sudden death, significant injury, persistent symptoms, recurrent unexplained events or concerning neurologic/metabolic findings; PICU for instability or malignant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward for exertional/supine syncope, abnormal ECG, known heart disease, family history of sudden death, significant injury, persistent symptoms, recurrent unexplained events or concerning neurologic/metabolic findings; PICU for instability or malignant arrhythmia.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; obtain orthostatic HR/BP when safe and clinically relevant.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Telemetry for cardiac red flags/abnormal ECG; fall precautions; neuro checks if head injury or incomplete recovery.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; oxygen for hypoxemia or cardiopulmonary cause.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Not routine for classic vasovagal syncope; obtain for dehydration, abnormal labs, recurrent event or concerning cause.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral hydration and salt when vasovagal/orthostatic pattern; isotonic IV fluid for clinically significant dehydration; regular diet unless procedure planned.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Bedside glucose and pregnancy test when applicable; CBC/electrolytes/toxicology only when suggested by history/exam. Do not order indiscriminate panels.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine neuroimaging. Echocardiography for abnormal exam/ECG, exertional syncope or cardiac history; head imaging only for significant trauma or neurologic concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; stop/review QT-prolonging or hypotensive medications; no empiric antiseizure or cardiac medication for uncomplicated vasovagal syncope.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology for exertional/supine episodes, abnormal ECG, palpitations, family history or structural disease; neurology only when seizure/neurologic disorder remains likely.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Document prodrome, position, duration, colour, movements and recovery; supervised ambulation until stable; hydration tracking.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review ECG personally and reassess before discharge planning. Recurrent event on monitor, ventricular arrhythmia, long QT/Brugada/WPW pattern, chest pain, dyspnea or persistent neurologic deficit requires urgent escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; oxygen for hypoxemia or cardiopulmonary cause.
Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; stop/review QT-prolonging or hypotensive medications; no empiric antiseizure or cardiac medication for uncomplicated vasovagal syncope.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Myocarditis / pericarditis
summary: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, hypotension, rising lactate, respiratory distress, altered mental status, or significant pericardial effusion/tamponade concern.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, hypotension, rising lactate, respiratory distress, altered mental status, or significant pericardial effusion/tamponade concern.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially, then q2-4h only after stability is clear.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous telemetry and pulse oximetry; strict I&O, perfusion, chest pain, hepatomegaly, and rhythm trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; use positive pressure cautiously in severe cardiac dysfunction and involve PICU.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second line if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Avoid routine fluid boluses unless clear hypovolemia; use cautious isotonic fluids with repeated cardiac assessment. Sodium/fluid restriction if heart failure.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Troponin, BNP/NT-proBNP, CBC, electrolytes including magnesium, renal/liver profile, CRP/ESR, gas/lactate if ill; infectious/autoimmune tests with cardiology.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG and echocardiogram; chest radiograph; cardiac MRI when stable and recommended by cardiology.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Activity restriction; treat heart failure/arrhythmia per cardiology; anti-inflammatory therapy for uncomplicated pericarditis when appropriate; avoid unnecessary catecholamine-provoking medications. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology urgently; PICU early for dysfunction/arrhythmia; rheumatology/ID when etiology requires.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Telemetry review, strict fluid balance, chest pain/rhythm documentation, minimal exertion, and immediate reporting of syncope or perfusion change.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess frequently with repeat ECG/biomarkers/echo as directed; escalate for ventricular arrhythmia, heart block, hypotension, rising lactate, worsening hepatomegaly, pulmonary edema, muffled heart sounds, or pulsus/tamponade features.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen as needed; use positive pressure cautiously in severe cardiac dysfunction and involve PICU.

Medications/treatments: Activity restriction; treat heart failure/arrhythmia per cardiology; anti-inflammatory therapy for uncomplicated pericarditis when appropriate; avoid unnecessary catecholamine-provoking medications. Verify doses.

title: Heart failure / congenital heart disease decompensation
summary: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for significant oxygen/support above baseline, shock, severe work of breathing, altered mental status, arrhythmia, duct-dependent physiology concern, or escalating diuretics/inotropes.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to cardiology/monitored unit; PICU for significant oxygen/support above baseline, shock, severe work of breathing, altered mental status, arrhythmia, duct-dependent physiology concern, or escalating diuretics/inotropes.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h until trajectory is clear; include pre/post-ductal saturations in infants when relevant and compare with baseline targets.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, strict I&O, daily weight, perfusion, hepatomegaly, feeding tolerance, and respiratory effort.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Use the child-specific oxygen saturation target; excessive oxygen may be harmful in selected mixing lesions. Continue verified home oxygen/NIV and involve RT/cardiology.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; second access if unstable. Avoid excessive agitation in fragile physiology.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Follow cardiac fluid/sodium plan; consider NPO with IV fluids if severe distress, but avoid both dehydration and fluid overload. Feeding support for infants with increased work.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, electrolytes/renal/liver profile, glucose, blood gas/lactate if ill, BNP/NT-proBNP as useful; drug levels when indicated; cultures if infection may have triggered decompensation.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: ECG, chest radiograph, echocardiogram per cardiology; device interrogation when relevant.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Continue verified essential cardiac medications unless contraindicated; diuretics/afterload/inotrope therapy per cardiology; treat trigger such as infection or anemia. Verify all doses and home formulation.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Cardiology immediately; PICU for any instability; cardiac surgery/device team when relevant; dietitian/feeding team for chronic growth issues.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Document baseline saturation/support, medication times, weights, urine output, feeds, hepatomegaly, edema, and parent-reported early signs of decompensation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after each intervention and at least q2h initially; escalate for worsening cyanosis, weak pulses, rising lactate, oliguria, new gallop, arrhythmia, increasing hepatomegaly, apnea, or support above unit capability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Use the child-specific oxygen saturation target; excessive oxygen may be harmful in selected mixing lesions. Continue verified home oxygen/NIV and involve RT/cardiology.

Medications/treatments: Continue verified essential cardiac medications unless contraindicated; diuretics/afterload/inotrope therapy per cardiology; treat trigger such as infection or anemia. Verify all doses and home formulation.

title: Rhabdomyolysis
summary: Admit for significant CK elevation with symptoms, pigmenturia, AKI/electrolyte abnormality, inability to hydrate orally, ongoing muscle injury or high-risk cause; PICU for severe hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, shock or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for significant CK elevation with symptoms, pigmenturia, AKI/electrolyte abnormality, inability to hydrate orally, ongoing muscle injury or high-risk cause; PICU for severe hyperkalemia, arrhythmia, shock or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q1-2h during severe electrolyte abnormality or aggressive fluid therapy.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict intake/output with urine output target, daily weight, serial limb/neurovascular exams and cardiac monitoring when potassium is abnormal.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support systemic cause/toxidrome as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for isotonic fluids and serial labs.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Start isotonic IV crystalloid, commonly 1.5-2 times maintenance and titrate to urine output/clinical status; avoid potassium-containing fluids initially. Routine bicarbonate/mannitol is not recommended without a specific indication.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CK, electrolytes including potassium/calcium/phosphate, urea/creatinine, bicarbonate, urinalysis, AST/ALT; ECG for hyperkalemia. Repeat CK/electrolytes/renal function q6-12h initially based on severity.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routine; ultrasound/MRI/compartment-pressure evaluation for focal trauma, infection or compartment syndrome.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Stop offending drug/exertion, treat hyperthermia/seizure/infection, manage hyperkalemia immediately using emergency protocol, avoid nephrotoxins/NSAIDs.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Nephrology for AKI, refractory electrolyte abnormality or dialysis concern; surgery/orthopedics for compartment syndrome; toxicology/metabolic genetics for relevant cause.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Accurate urine output/colour, fluid-balance and limb pain/swelling checks; avoid potassium supplements and nephrotoxins.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Trend CK, potassium, creatinine and urine output. Oliguria, rising potassium/creatinine, ECG change, severe hypocalcemic symptoms or tense painful compartment requires urgent escalation.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: None routinely; support systemic cause/toxidrome as needed.
Medications/treatments: Stop offending drug/exertion, treat hyperthermia/seizure/infection, manage hyperkalemia immediately using emergency protocol, avoid nephrotoxins/NSAIDs.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Anaphylaxis
summary: Admit/observe in a monitored setting after stabilization; PICU for shock, airway edema, repeated epinephrine, ongoing bronchospasm, arrhythmia, or need for epinephrine infusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit/observe in a monitored setting after stabilization; PICU for shock, airway edema, repeated epinephrine, ongoing bronchospasm, arrhythmia, or need for epinephrine infusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous monitoring during active symptoms; repeat BP, perfusion, respiratory and skin assessment every 5-15 min until clearly stable, then space according to risk.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiac monitoring; strict documentation of epinephrine times, BP and symptom response.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen, airway positioning and early difficult-airway planning for voice change, stridor, tongue/oropharyngeal swelling, or progressive obstruction; inhaled salbutamol for persistent bronchospasm after epinephrine.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly for moderate-severe reaction; two IVs/IO if shock.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO during airway risk. For persistent hypotension give isotonic crystalloid 20 mL/kg rapidly and reassess; repeat judiciously while preparing vasoactive support.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Diagnosis is clinical; no routine labs. Consider tryptase according to allergy pathway without delaying treatment; obtain gas/lactate/electrolytes if shock.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: IM epinephrine 1 mg/mL (1:1000) at 0.01 mg/kg = 0.01 mL/kg into anterolateral thigh (max 0.5 mg), repeat every 5-15 min as needed. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts only and must never delay epinephrine. Start titrated IV epinephrine infusion in refractory shock with PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Senior/RT immediately; PICU/anesthesia for airway or circulatory compromise; allergy referral before discharge planning.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Keep epinephrine and airway cart at bedside; lay flat with legs elevated unless respiratory distress/vomiting; do not allow sudden standing; record likely trigger and biphasic-risk features.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess 5 min after each epinephrine dose. Observe at least 4-6 h after symptom resolution, longer/overnight for severe reaction, delayed epinephrine, multiple doses, asthma, remote access, or biphasic-risk factors.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-flow oxygen, airway positioning and early difficult-airway planning for voice change, stridor, tongue/oropharyngeal swelling, or progressive obstruction; inhaled salbutamol for persistent bronchospasm after epinephrine.

Medications/treatments: IM epinephrine 1 mg/mL (1:1000) at 0.01 mg/kg = 0.01 mL/kg into anterolateral thigh (max 0.5 mg), repeat every 5-15 min as needed. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts only and must never delay epinephrine. Start titrated IV epinephrine infusion in refractory shock with PICU.

title: Allergic reaction without anaphylaxis
summary: Admit to Ward observation if stable; upgrade immediately if any respiratory/circulatory involvement or multisystem progression.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward observation if stable; upgrade immediately if any respiratory/circulatory involvement or multisystem progression.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Routine vitals; pulse oximetry if facial swelling/asthma; repeated airway/system assessment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: None unless wheeze/airway change.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Usually none.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Oral fluids.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Usually none; targeted complement/tryptase or other tests are not routine overnight.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine for bothersome urticaria; corticosteroid only for selected indications. Epinephrine if anaphylaxis develops.

sections.label: Consults

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Mark/photograph rash per consent/policy, monitor voice/swallow/breathing and progression.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Reassess within 30–60 minutes and before discharge.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: None unless wheeze/airway change.

title: Ingestion or overdose
summary: Admit to a monitored ward for stable low-to-moderate risk after a poison-centre plan is established; use PICU for airway or ventilation support, hemodynamic instability, severe toxidrome, antidote infusion, seizure, significant ECG abnormality, or extracorporeal therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to a monitored ward for stable low-to-moderate risk after a poison-centre plan is established; use PICU for airway or ventilation support, hemodynamic instability, severe toxidrome, antidote infusion, seizure, significant ECG abnormality, or extracorporeal therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory/SpO₂ for cardiotoxic/sedating agents; serial ECG and targeted labs; neuro checks; 1:1 safety for intentional ingestion.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Ventilation support; avoid unprotected charcoal.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV access; IO if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Cause-directed; avoid routine large boluses if cardiotoxicity unless indicated; correct glucose/electrolytes.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Point-of-care glucose, ECG, acetaminophen concentration at appropriate time for all plausible intentional/unknown ingestions, and agent-specific labs (salicylate, gas, electrolytes, CK, osmolality, pregnancy, etc.) per poison centre.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Source-directed; body-packer/foreign-body imaging only with expert plan.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Call provincial poison centre early. Use specific antidote/decontamination only when indicated; activated charcoal requires protected airway and correct timing. Treat seizures, dysrhythmias and sodium-channel blockade per toxicology protocol.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Poison centre/toxicology; PICU; psychiatry/social work after medically stable for intentional ingestion; child protection for unsafe exposure.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Secure belongings/medications, 1:1 as indicated, exact serial ECG/lab times, avoid discharge before toxic observation window.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Continuous in symptomatic/high-risk; repeat ECG/labs at poison-centre intervals; reassess after every intervention.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Ventilation support; avoid unprotected charcoal.

Medications/treatments: Call provincial poison centre early. Use specific antidote/decontamination only when indicated; activated charcoal requires protected airway and correct timing. Treat seizures, dysrhythmias and sodium-channel blockade per toxicology protocol.

title: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) overdose
summary: Call the Ontario Poison Centre immediately (1-800-268-9017). Stabilize ABCs and glucose, determine the earliest possible ingestion time and formulation, obtain an acetaminophen level at 4 hours or later with hepatic/renal assessment, start IV acetylcysteine promptly when indicated, and use scheduled laboratory monitoring until Poison Centre stopping criteria are met.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit patients receiving IV acetylcysteine (NAC), with a toxic concentration, delayed or unknown-time ingestion, repeated supratherapeutic ingestion, elevated AST/ALT or INR, persistent vomiting, clinically important co-ingestion, intentional ingestion requiring safety assessment, or unreliable follow-up. PICU and early pediatric liver/transplant-centre discussion are required for altered mental status/encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis or rising lactate, shock, rapidly worsening INR, acute kidney injury/oliguria, clinically important bleeding, or other evidence of acute liver failure.

sections.label: Immediate stabilization and history
sections.text: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, neurologic status and bedside glucose; obtain measured weight in kg and reliable IV access. Treat hypoglycemia, seizures, shock, acidosis or respiratory failure immediately. Document exact product/concentration, immediate- versus extended-release formulation, maximum possible amount in mg and mg/kg, exact or earliest possible ingestion time, single ingestion versus doses spread over time, vomiting, opioid/anticholinergic or other co-ingestants, intentionality, fasting/malnutrition/eating disorder, liver disease and treatment before arrival. Use the earliest possible time as time zero. Do not induce vomiting.

sections.label: Decontamination
sections.text: Discuss activated charcoal with Ontario Poison Centre. Consider single-dose activated charcoal for a potentially toxic ingestion when presentation is early enough to provide benefit and the airway is protected with no bowel obstruction or major aspiration risk. Poison Centre may recommend charcoal later after a massive ingestion, extended-release product or opioid/anticholinergic co-ingestion because absorption may be delayed. Never delay NAC when NAC is indicated.

sections.label: Initial investigations
sections.text: Obtain acetaminophen concentration, AST, ALT, PT/INR, sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, glucose, urea/BUN, creatinine, VBG and lactate. Add bilirubin, salicylate concentration, ethanol/measured osmolality, beta-hCG and ECG when clinically appropriate or the ingestion is intentional/uncertain. The definitive acetaminophen concentration must be collected at least 4 hours after an acute ingestion; a level obtained earlier cannot exclude toxicity and must be repeated at 4 hours.

sections.label: Risk assessment and nomogram
sections.text: Use the Rumack-Matthew nomogram only for a single acute ingestion with a known time, a concentration drawn at least 4 hours after ingestion, and presentation within 24 hours. Plot using the earliest possible ingestion time. Start NAC when the concentration is on or above the treatment line. Do not use the nomogram for unknown time, repeated supratherapeutic ingestion, presentation beyond 24 hours or established hepatic injury. If the reported time is a range and the initial level is below the treatment line, repeat a level 4 hours after the latest possible ingestion time before excluding treatment. Extended-release products and delayed gastric emptying require serial levels.

sections.label: When to start NAC
sections.text: Start IV NAC when the timed level is on/above the treatment line; when a potentially toxic acute ingestion occurred and the level will not be available before 8 hours after ingestion; when timing is unknown and acetaminophen is detectable; when AST/ALT is elevated with possible acetaminophen exposure; in repeated supratherapeutic ingestion with a concerning level or liver injury; in delayed presentation with suspected acetaminophen-related hepatic injury even if the level is low/undetectable; or whenever Poison Centre recommends empiric therapy. Do not delay NAC while awaiting investigations in a late or high-risk presentation.

sections.label: IV acetylcysteine dosing
sections.text: Use the current Ontario Poison Centre protocol and hospital order set; involve pharmacy. Prepare NAC as a 3% solution (30 mg/mL) in D5W, normal saline or half-normal saline. Loading: 150 mg/kg IV over 1 hour (5 mL/kg of 3% solution). Immediately follow with maintenance: 15 mg/kg/hour continuously (0.5 mL/kg/hour of 3% solution). Use maximum dosing weight 100 kg. Continue until every stopping criterion is met and Poison Centre approves discontinuation; do not stop automatically after a fixed number of hours. At least 12 total hours of NAC, including the loading dose, must be given before routine stopping criteria are assessed.

sections.label: Routine monitoring and exact laboratory timing
sections.text: Stable patient on NAC: vitals and neurologic status q4h; continuous cardiorespiratory and pulse-oximetry monitoring during the loading dose and whenever unstable; strict intake/output. Obtain baseline acetaminophen concentration, AST/ALT, PT/INR, electrolytes/bicarbonate, glucose, urea/BUN, creatinine, VBG and lactate. Repeat this complete panel EVERY 12 HOURS while NAC is running. Example: NAC starts 20:00 -> repeat full panel at approximately 08:00 while infusion continues. Do not stop NAC while results are pending. Check bedside glucose immediately for lethargy, confusion, diaphoresis, seizure, hypotension or deterioration.

sections.label: High-risk, delayed absorption and liver-injury monitoring
sections.text: For extended-release ingestion, opioid/anticholinergic co-ingestion, massive tablet ingestion or delayed gastric emptying: repeat acetaminophen concentration EVERY 4 HOURS until it has clearly peaked, then every 12 hours until below 66 micromol/L (10 mg/L). For high-risk overdose, significant hepatic injury or clinical deterioration: repeat acetaminophen concentration, VBG, lactate, electrolytes/bicarbonate, glucose, urea/BUN, creatinine, AST/ALT and PT/INR EVERY 4 HOURS until improving or Poison Centre changes the schedule; add phosphate and lipase when indicated. With altered mental status, hypoglycemia or evolving liver failure, check bedside glucose EVERY 1-2 HOURS (hourly if severe). Check phosphate every 12 hours with hepatic injury, or every 4-6 hours if severely low or being actively replaced. Repeat labs immediately rather than waiting for schedule after any clinical deterioration.

sections.label: NAC reaction and supportive care
sections.text: During NAC loading watch for flushing, pruritus, urticaria, angioedema, wheeze, vomiting and hypotension. If a reaction occurs, pause the infusion, assess ABCs, treat bronchospasm/hypotension/anaphylaxis physiology as indicated, give antihistamine for isolated cutaneous symptoms when appropriate, and call Poison Centre. Restart NAC at the advised rate once symptoms resolve; a manageable reaction is not usually a reason to permanently discontinue NAC. Give regular diet/oral fluids if well; use isotonic IV fluids for poor intake and dextrose for hypoglycemia. Avoid further acetaminophen and unnecessary hepatotoxic medications. Do not give plasma solely to normalize INR unless there is important bleeding, a necessary procedure, or specialist advice.

sections.label: Stopping criteria
sections.text: Never stop NAC solely because 12, 20 or 21 hours have elapsed. If NAC was started for a level above the treatment line or because the nomogram could not be used, ALL must be true: acetaminophen below 66 micromol/L (10 mg/L); AST or ALT <=100 IU/L, or if >100 IU/L then falling and now <50% of peak; INR <2; patient clinically stable; at least 12 total hours of NAC completed; and Poison Centre agrees. If NAC was started before the level resulted, ALL must be true: level plots below treatment line, AST/ALT below local upper limit of normal, INR <2, delayed absorption excluded and Poison Centre agrees. If treatment was started only from history because levels were unavailable, continue at least 24 hours and discuss before stopping.

sections.label: Consults, safety and escalation
sections.text: Call Ontario Poison Centre for every significant or uncertain ingestion and pharmacy for NAC preparation. For intentional overdose, institute suicide precautions, secure medications/unsafe belongings and arrange mental-health/social-work assessment after medical stabilization. Notify senior physician, Poison Centre, PICU, hepatology and a pediatric liver/transplant centre urgently for encephalopathy, recurrent hypoglycemia, worsening acidosis or lactate, hypotension, INR >=2 or rapidly increasing, rapidly rising AST/ALT, bleeding, AKI/oliguria, severe hypophosphatemia or any deterioration despite NAC. Continue NAC during escalation; specialized therapy such as fomepizole, intensified NAC or extracorporeal treatment requires toxicology/Poison Centre direction.

treatments.text: NAC 3% solution: 150 mg/kg IV over 1 hour, then 15 mg/kg/hour continuously. Continue until Poison Centre confirms all stopping criteria are met.
Baseline and every 12 hours while on NAC: acetaminophen concentration, VBG, lactate, electrolytes/bicarbonate, glucose, urea/BUN, creatinine, AST, ALT and PT/INR.

Every 4 hours for delayed absorption, high-risk overdose, hepatic injury or deterioration: acetaminophen concentration, VBG, lactate, electrolytes, glucose, renal function, AST/ALT and INR; bedside glucose every 1-2 hours if liver failure is possible.

guidance: Ontario Poison Centre acetaminophen resources and IV acetylcysteine protocol effective April 1, 2026. Call 1-800-268-9017 and verify the current local order set.

title: Opioid or sedative ingestion
summary: Admit to monitored ward for recurrent sedation, long-acting agent, repeated naloxone, uncertain ingestion, co-ingestion or safeguarding concern; PICU for apnea, airway support or naloxone infusion.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored ward for recurrent sedation, long-acting agent, repeated naloxone, uncertain ingestion, co-ingestion or safeguarding concern; PICU for apnea, airway support or naloxone infusion.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous during respiratory depression; q15-30 min after naloxone until stable, then q2-4h through the expected drug duration.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring; capnography when available; frequent sedation score and pupils.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Airway positioning, oxygen and bag-mask ventilation are first priorities. Prepare intubation if ventilation cannot be maintained.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for moderate-severe symptoms; IO if unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO until fully awake; isotonic fluids only as needed.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Bedside glucose, gas if hypoventilating, electrolytes and targeted levels/co-ingestion tests (including acetaminophen) based on history. Routine urine drug screen rarely changes acute care.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph if aspiration/pulmonary edema; neuroimaging only for trauma/focal signs/nonresponse.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Naloxone IV/IM/IN titrated to adequate ventilation; use 0.1 mg/kg (max 2 mg) in children or opioid-naive patients with severe respiratory depression, with smaller titrated doses in opioid-dependent adolescents. Repeat as needed; start infusion when recurrent depression occurs after effective bolus, with toxicology/PICU.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Poison Centre/toxicology; PICU/anesthesia for airway or infusion; child protection for unsafe exposure; mental health for intentional ingestion.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Continuous observation, suction/bag-mask/naloxone at bedside, record response duration after each dose, secure belongings and medications.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Reassess ventilation within minutes after naloxone and observe beyond the antagonist duration. Recurrent bradypnea, hypercapnia or sedation requires repeat naloxone/infusion and PICU.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Airway positioning, oxygen and bag-mask ventilation are first priorities. Prepare intubation if ventilation cannot be maintained.

Medications/treatments: Naloxone IV/IM/IN titrated to adequate ventilation; use 0.1 mg/kg (max 2 mg) in children or opioid-naive patients with severe respiratory depression, with smaller titrated doses in opioid-dependent adolescents. Repeat as needed; start infusion when recurrent depression occurs after effective bolus, with toxicology/PICU.

title: Smoke inhalation / carbon monoxide exposure
summary: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for altered mental status, airway edema, significant respiratory distress, hemodynamic instability, severe metabolic acidosis, neurologic symptoms, or need for advanced airway/hyperbaric consultation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to monitored CTU/step-down; PICU for altered mental status, airway edema, significant respiratory distress, hemodynamic instability, severe metabolic acidosis, neurologic symptoms, or need for advanced airway/hyperbaric consultation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; continuous observation during high-flow oxygen and for evolving airway injury.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and pulse oximetry, recognizing that standard pulse oximetry does not measure carboxyhemoglobin; serial neurologic and airway examinations.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Give high-concentration oxygen immediately; early anesthesia/ENT/PICU for facial burns, soot, hoarseness, stridor, progressive swelling, or enclosed-space exposure. Do not delay airway control for imaging.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; consider second line for significant burns, shock, or antidotal therapy.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO if airway injury is possible; isotonic fluids based on perfusion and burn needs, avoiding over-resuscitation.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Co-oximetry/carboxyhemoglobin, blood gas/lactate, glucose, electrolytes/renal function, CBC; cyanide evaluation/treatment based on exposure and severe lactate/shock after toxicology consultation.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Chest radiograph for respiratory symptoms; bronchoscopy or additional imaging only with specialists. Initial chest radiograph may be normal.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Give 100% oxygen by non-rebreather immediately; do not rely on pulse oximetry. Treat bronchospasm and thermal airway injury; discuss hyperbaric oxygen urgently for severe symptoms, neurologic findings, cardiac ischemia/arrhythmia, significant acidosis, pregnancy or high COHb according to Poison Centre/hyperbaric service.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Poison centre/toxicology, PICU/anesthesia early for airway or neurologic concern, burn service, hyperbaric medicine according to regional criteria.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT: Serial voice/stridor/secretions, neurologic checks, oxygen-device integrity, burn assessment, and exact exposure history/time.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess airway and neurologic status frequently; escalate for increasing hoarseness/stridor, soot-laden secretions, rising work of breathing, syncope, seizure, confusion, acidosis, or hemodynamic instability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Give high-concentration oxygen immediately; early anesthesia/ENT/PICU for facial burns, soot, hoarseness, stridor, progressive swelling, or enclosed-space exposure. Do not delay airway control for imaging.

Medications/treatments: Give 100% oxygen by non-rebreather immediately; do not rely on pulse oximetry. Treat bronchospasm and thermal airway injury; discuss hyperbaric oxygen urgently for severe symptoms, neurologic findings, cardiac ischemia/arrhythmia, significant acidosis, pregnancy or high COHb according to Poison Centre/hyperbaric service.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Failure to thrive / growth faltering
summary: Admit to Ward for stable diagnostic/nutritional admission; PICU for shock, severe electrolyte abnormality, respiratory failure or cardiac compromise.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for stable diagnostic/nutritional admission; PICU for shock, severe electrolyte abnormality, respiratory failure or cardiac compromise.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Daily weight under standardized conditions, strict intake/output, observed feeding, calorie count; cardiorespiratory monitoring if severe malnutrition/refeeding risk.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support if aspiration/respiratory disease; feeding route guided by safety.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV only for dehydration/critical labs; NG may be preferred for nutrition.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Correct deficit carefully; nutrition advancement with phosphate/potassium/magnesium/thiamine plan when severe malnutrition.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Targeted CBC, electrolytes, glucose, renal/liver tests, calcium/magnesium/phosphate, urinalysis, thyroid/celiac/stool tests based on presentation; avoid indiscriminate panels.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Only cause-directed.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; structured feeding/nutrition plan; vitamin/mineral replacement and refeeding prophylaxis per dietitian/local guideline.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Dietitian, social work, feeding/SLP/OT, lactation, GI/endocrine/cardiology and child protection as indicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Document exact intake and feed behavior, caregiver teaching, weights and emesis/stool; monitor for edema/arrhythmia during refeeding.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Review feed tolerance each feed; daily weight; refeeding electrolytes q6–24 h based on risk.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support if aspiration/respiratory disease; feeding route guided by safety.
Medications/treatments: Treat identified cause; structured feeding/nutrition plan; vitamin/mineral replacement and refeeding prophylaxis per dietitian/local guideline.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Eating disorder - medical stabilization
summary: Admit to adolescent medicine/CTU for medical instability, significant bradycardia/hypotension/orthostasis, hypothermia, electrolyte abnormality, dehydration, acute food refusal, syncope, arrhythmia, or high refeeding risk; PICU for unstable rhythm, shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, or altered mental status.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to adolescent medicine/CTU for medical instability, significant bradycardia/hypotension/orthostasis, hypothermia, electrolyte abnormality, dehydration, acute food refusal, syncope, arrhythmia, or high refeeding risk; PICU for unstable rhythm, shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, or altered mental status.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Resting and orthostatic vitals per pathway; q4h if stable, more frequently for significant instability. Avoid repeated unnecessary exertion.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiac monitoring when marked bradycardia, QT concern, electrolyte abnormality, or syncope; strict I&O, daily blinded weight, temperature, and refeeding symptoms.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for heart failure or respiratory muscle weakness in severe malnutrition.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Avoid routine IV fluids unless clinically dehydrated or unstable; obtain access for significant electrolyte treatment or inability to hydrate orally.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Start structured nutrition/refeeding protocol with supervised meals and prescribed fluid limits; avoid unplanned fluid loading and monitor for edema.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Electrolytes including phosphate/magnesium/potassium, glucose, renal/liver profile, CBC, urinalysis; ECG; repeat refeeding labs at pathway-defined intervals. Pregnancy and other tests as appropriate.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Not routinely required; bone or other imaging only for specific indications.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Replace electrolytes and vitamins per pathway; avoid QT-prolonging or hypotension-worsening drugs where possible; manage constipation cautiously. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Adolescent medicine/eating-disorder team, dietitian, psychiatry/psychology, social work; cardiology/PICU for significant cardiac instability.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Supervised meals/post-meal observation, activity restriction, bathroom supervision when indicated, blinded weights, intake documentation, and nonjudgmental communication.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess vitals, ECG, glucose, and refeeding electrolytes as scheduled; escalate for syncope, chest pain, arrhythmia, worsening bradycardia/hypotension, hypoglycemia, rapidly falling phosphate/potassium/magnesium, edema with respiratory symptoms, or acute suicidality.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Not routinely required; assess for heart failure or respiratory muscle weakness in severe malnutrition.
Medications/treatments: Replace electrolytes and vitamins per pathway; avoid QT-prolonging or hypotension-worsening drugs where possible; manage constipation cautiously. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Safeguarding / suspected non-accidental injury
summary: Admit when medical observation or investigation is required, or when safety cannot be assured. Use PICU/trauma/neurosurgery for physiologic instability or serious injury, and do not discharge to an unsafe setting.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit when medical observation or investigation is required, or when safety cannot be assured. Use PICU/trauma/neurosurgery for physiologic instability or serious injury, and do not discharge to an unsafe setting.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Monitoring based on injuries; neuro checks for head injury; strict I&O for abdominal/renal injury; 1:1 safety if required.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support based on injury.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if injured/unstable; minimize unnecessary procedures that may affect evidence while prioritizing care.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Cause/injury-directed.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC, coagulation, liver/pancreatic enzymes, urinalysis, toxicology, STI/pregnancy testing and bone-health labs as directed by child-protection pathway.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Skeletal survey in indicated young children, neuroimaging/ophthalmology for abusive head trauma concern, abdominal imaging for occult injury—coordinate with child protection/radiology.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat injuries, pain and infections; provide prophylaxis after sexual exposure when indicated with specialist guidance.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Child protection team/social work immediately; report to child-welfare authority as legally required; trauma, neurosurgery, ophthalmology, SANE/sexual-assault team, police through protocol.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Use exact quotes, objective measurements and times; preserve clothing/specimens with chain of custody; restrict information sharing to appropriate teams.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Medical reassessment according to injury; safety huddle before any leave/discharge; ensure sibling risk considered.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support based on injury.
Medications/treatments: Treat injuries, pain and infections; provide prophylaxis after sexual exposure when indicated with specialist guidance.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Burn injury
summary: Admit to burn/trauma/CTU for partial/full-thickness burns requiring inpatient wound care, significant TBSA, high-risk location, circumferential injury, inhalation/electrical/chemical burn, pain-control failure, safeguarding concern, or unreliable follow-up; PICU for airway, shock, major TBSA, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to burn/trauma/CTU for partial/full-thickness burns requiring inpatient wound care, significant TBSA, high-risk location, circumferential injury, inhalation/electrical/chemical burn, pain-control failure, safeguarding concern, or unreliable follow-up; PICU for airway, shock, major TBSA, or organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q2-4h for stable minor admissions; q1h during resuscitation or airway concern.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Pain, perfusion, temperature, urine output, distal neurovascular status for circumferential burns, and respiratory/airway signs; continuous monitoring if significant burn or opioids.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: High-concentration oxygen for smoke exposure; early airway control for evolving inhalation injury. Keep child warm.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain away from burned tissue when possible; two lines for major burns. Intraosseous access if emergent.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Oral fluids for small burns when tolerated; formal weight/TBSA-based resuscitation for major burns with burn-service guidance and urine-output targets; early enteral nutrition for major burns.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: None routinely for small burns; CBC, electrolytes/renal function, gas/lactate, CK, co-oximetry, glucose and type/screen for major, electrical, inhalation, or traumatic burns.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Trauma- or exposure-directed; ECG and serial labs for electrical injury; chest imaging for inhalation/trauma as indicated.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Analgesia, cleansing/debridement/dressing per burn pathway, tetanus review, topical therapy as directed; systemic antibiotics only for established infection, not prophylaxis. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Burn/plastics, trauma/surgery, PICU/anesthesia for airway/major burns, ophthalmology for ocular exposure, child protection when mechanism is concerning.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Warm environment, wound/dressing plan, pain/sedation scoring, neurovascular checks, fluid-balance documentation, and safeguarding documentation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after analgesia/dressing and frequently during resuscitation; escalate for stridor/hoarseness, worsening perfusion, compartment signs, dark urine after electrical injury, hypothermia, oliguria, or resuscitation needs above ward capability.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: High-concentration oxygen for smoke exposure; early airway control for evolving inhalation injury. Keep child warm.

Medications/treatments: Analgesia, cleansing/debridement/dressing per burn pathway, tetanus review, topical therapy as directed; systemic antibiotics only for established infection, not prophylaxis. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Blunt trauma / solid organ injury
summary: Admit under trauma/surgery; CTU only for hemodynamically stable injury with a defined nonoperative plan; PICU for shock, ongoing transfusion, significant head/chest injury, respiratory support, or high-grade/multisystem trauma.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit under trauma/surgery; CTU only for hemodynamically stable injury with a defined nonoperative plan; PICU for shock, ongoing transfusion, significant head/chest injury, respiratory support, or high-grade/multisystem trauma.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q1-2h initially; frequency set by trauma grade and stability.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring for significant injury; serial abdominal/neurovascular/neurologic examinations, pain, urine output, and bleeding signs.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; maintain cervical-spine precautions until cleared; early airway control for deterioration.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Two large-bore IVs for significant injury; type and cross. Avoid delays in blood products for hemorrhagic shock.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: NPO initially; balanced resuscitation using blood products when hemorrhage is suspected and avoiding excessive crystalloid; advance diet only per trauma plan.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: CBC serially when indicated, type/cross, coagulation/fibrinogen, electrolytes/renal/liver profile, lipase, urinalysis, blood gas/lactate; pregnancy testing when relevant.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: FAST/ultrasound and CT according to trauma pathway and stability; do not send an unstable child to CT before resuscitation/surgical decision.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Analgesia without masking deterioration, antiemetic, tetanus/wound care, transfusion/hemostatic therapy per trauma pathway. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Trauma/surgery immediately; PICU, neurosurgery, orthopedics, urology, interventional radiology, and child protection as injuries dictate.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Serial vital/abdominal/neurovascular checks, NPO, strict I&O, document bruising/injury pattern accurately, and maintain spinal precautions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after every intervention and at the trauma-defined interval; escalate for increasing pain/distension, tachycardia, hypotension, falling hemoglobin, peritonitis, reduced urine output, respiratory decline, or altered mental status.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/support as needed; maintain cervical-spine precautions until cleared; early airway control for deterioration.
Medications/treatments: Analgesia without masking deterioration, antiemetic, tetanus/wound care, transfusion/hemostatic therapy per trauma pathway. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Neonatal jaundice / unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
summary: Admit to a mother-baby unit or pediatric ward capable of intensive phototherapy; use NICU/PICU for acute bilirubin encephalopathy, bilirubin at or approaching the exchange-transfusion threshold, or need for intensive cardiorespiratory support.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to a mother-baby unit or pediatric ward capable of intensive phototherapy; use NICU/PICU for acute bilirubin encephalopathy, bilirubin at or approaching the exchange-transfusion threshold, or need for intensive cardiorespiratory support.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Temperature, feeding/urine/stool, daily weight; bilirubin at guideline-timed intervals; cardiorespiratory monitoring if exchange-level illness or unstable.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as required; maintain thermoregulation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if exchange escalation, significant dehydration, sepsis or unable to feed.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Optimize enteral intake; IV isotonic/glucose fluid only for indication.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Total and direct bilirubin, blood group/DAT, CBC/retic/smear and G6PD/hemolysis tests when indicated; albumin and crossmatch near exchange threshold; sepsis evaluation if ill.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: No routine imaging; direct hyperbilirubinemia requires cholestasis evaluation.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Plot total bilirubin against age in hours and gestational-age/neurotoxicity-risk thresholds. Start intensive phototherapy at the CPS 2025 treatment threshold; arrange exchange transfusion/PICU-neonatal transfer for bilirubin at/near exchange threshold or acute bilirubin encephalopathy. Continue feeding support and treat hemolysis/sepsis.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neonatology urgently near exchange threshold or neuro signs; transfusion medicine; hematology for hemolysis; lactation.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Maximize skin exposure/eye protection/thermoregulation, document irradiance, feeds/output and interruptions; obtain bilirubin at ordered times.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Repeat bilirubin at interval determined by distance to threshold/rate/risk; immediate reassessment for tone, cry, feeding or apnea change.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as required; maintain thermoregulation.

Medications/treatments: Plot total bilirubin against age in hours and gestational-age/neurotoxicity-risk thresholds. Start intensive phototherapy at the CPS 2025 treatment threshold; arrange exchange transfusion/PICU-neonatal transfer for bilirubin at/near exchange threshold or acute bilirubin encephalopathy. Continue feeding support and treat hemolysis/sepsis.

title: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia / neonatal cholestasis
summary: Admit to Ward for urgent evaluation; NICU/PICU for liver failure, sepsis, hypoglycemia, bleeding or encephalopathy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to Ward for urgent evaluation; NICU/PICU for liver failure, sepsis, hypoglycemia, bleeding or encephalopathy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q4h if stable; q2h initially for moderate/evolving illness; continuous monitoring or q15-60 min during active resuscitation or rapid change.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Vitals, glucose, intake/output, stool color and bleeding; cardiorespiratory monitoring if ill.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: IV if ill or significant coagulopathy/hypoglycemia.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids: Maintain glucose and nutrition; avoid fasting in metabolic concern.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Fractionated bilirubin, AST/ALT/GGT/ALP, albumin, glucose, coagulation/INR, CBC, cultures, metabolic/endocrine/infectious tests with GI; repeat newborn-screen review.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: Urgent abdominal ultrasound and further biliary imaging per GI/hepatology; do not let normal ultrasound falsely end evaluation if acholic stool.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat sepsis/metabolic emergency; vitamin K for deficiency/coagulopathy as directed; disease-specific therapy with specialist. Phototherapy does not treat conjugated bilirubin and may cause bronze discoloration.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: GI/hepatology urgently, especially acholic stool; surgery for biliary atresia pathway; metabolic/ID/endocrine as indicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing/RT instructions: Save/photograph stool color per policy, glucose checks, bleeding precautions and nutrition documentation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment timing: Frequent if ill; daily or specialist-directed liver/coagulation trend; expedite daytime definitive workup.

treatments.text: Respiratory support if needed: Support as needed.

Medications/treatments: Treat sepsis/metabolic emergency; vitamin K for deficiency/coagulopathy as directed; disease-specific therapy with specialist. Phototherapy does not treat conjugated bilirubin and may cause bronze discoloration.

title: Neonatal fever / suspected neonatal sepsis (0-28 days)
summary: Admit to NICU/CTU with immediate senior and neonatal expertise. Use NICU/PICU for ill appearance, apnea, shock, respiratory support, seizure, or suspected HSV with organ dysfunction.

title: Neonatal hypoglycemia
summary: Admit to newborn unit/CTU with neonatal expertise; NICU for symptomatic/recurrent hypoglycemia, need for high glucose infusion, seizures, respiratory instability, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, or inability to maintain glucose enterally.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to newborn unit/CTU with neonatal expertise; NICU for symptomatic/recurrent hypoglycemia, need for high glucose infusion, seizures, respiratory instability, suspected endocrine/metabolic disease, or inability to maintain glucose enterally.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q3-4h with feeds when stable; continuous observation for symptomatic infants.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Bedside glucose at pathway-defined times before/after feeds or infusion changes; temperature, feeding, neurologic status, urine output, and daily weight.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation for apnea, seizure, or severe illness; maintain thermoregulation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain promptly for symptomatic, very low, recurrent, or feed-unresponsive glucose; consider central access only if prolonged high-concentration glucose is required.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Immediate feeding if safe; breast milk/formula supplementation and feeding support per neonatal pathway; IV dextrose when symptomatic or not responding to enteral treatment.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Confirm plasma glucose when feasible without delaying treatment; critical sample during recurrent/persistent hypoglycemia before correction when safe; electrolytes, cortisol/GH/metabolic/endocrine studies with specialists.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; neuroimaging only for seizures/neurologic injury or another indication.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Feed promptly when safe. For asymptomatic low glucose in an eligible infant, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally with a feed may be used per newborn pathway. Symptomatic/persistent hypoglycemia requires IV D10W bolus/infusion per neonatal protocol and investigation for persistent disease.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Neonatology; endocrinology/metabolic genetics for persistent/recurrent disease; lactation/dietitian.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Timed glucose checks, feed volumes/duration, IV-site checks, thermoregulation, and immediate treatment of symptoms; independent verification of glucose infusion rate.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess glucose after every treatment/feed/infusion change; escalate for seizure, apnea, lethargy, recurrent low glucose, rising infusion requirement, or inability to obtain/maintain access.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support airway/ventilation for apnea, seizure, or severe illness; maintain thermoregulation.

Medications/treatments: Feed promptly when safe. For asymptomatic low glucose in an eligible infant, 40% dextrose gel 0.5 mL/kg buccally with a feed may be used per newborn pathway. Symptomatic/persistent hypoglycemia requires IV D10W bolus/infusion per neonatal protocol and investigation for persistent disease.

guidance: CPS: Screening and management of newborns at risk for low blood glucose.
