title: Poor feeding / excessive neonatal weight loss
summary: Admit to newborn unit/CTU for significant weight loss/dehydration, hypernatremia, hypoglycemia, jaundice requiring treatment, lethargy, temperature instability, unsafe feeding, or concern for infection/cardiac/metabolic disease; NICU for instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to newborn unit/CTU for significant weight loss/dehydration, hypernatremia, hypoglycemia, jaundice requiring treatment, lethargy, temperature instability, unsafe feeding, or concern for infection/cardiac/metabolic disease; NICU for instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: q3-4h with feeds; more frequently if dehydrated, hypothermic, hypoglycemic, or unwell.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Pre/post-feed assessment, intake, urine/stool count, daily weight, temperature, glucose and bilirubin as indicated; observe work of breathing and perfusion during feeds.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Support as needed; stop oral feeding and assess airway/swallow if coughing, cyanosis, tachypnea, or fatigue occurs with feeds.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Obtain for significant dehydration/hypernatremia, hypoglycemia, sepsis evaluation, or inability to feed safely.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Immediate individualized feeding plan with expressed breast milk/formula supplementation; correct dehydration/electrolytes gradually; involve lactation and use NG feeds when safe but oral intake is insufficient.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Glucose, sodium/electrolytes/renal function, total/direct bilirubin; CBC/cultures/gas and endocrine/metabolic/cardiac tests if clinical findings warrant.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: None routinely; chest/cardiac/abdominal imaging only for specific signs such as respiratory distress, murmur/poor perfusion, or bilious vomiting.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Treat hypoglycemia, jaundice, infection, or other identified cause; vitamin supplementation per newborn plan. Verify doses.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: Lactation, dietitian/feeding team, neonatology; cardiology, GI, SLP, endocrine/metabolic, or social work based on cause and feeding safety.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing: Detailed feed duration/volume/quality, urine/stool, daily naked weight on same scale, parent teaching, safe sleep, and signs of feeding fatigue.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess after each feed initially and repeat sodium/glucose/bilirubin as indicated; escalate for lethargy, apnea, poor perfusion, bilious emesis, worsening hypernatremia, recurrent hypoglycemia, fever/hypothermia, or inability to safely complete feeds.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Support as needed; stop oral feeding and assess airway/swallow if coughing, cyanosis, tachypnea, or fatigue occurs with feeds.
Medications/treatments: Treat hypoglycemia, jaundice, infection, or other identified cause; vitamin supplementation per newborn plan. Verify doses.

guidance: Standard pediatric inpatient practice; confirm the hospital order set, formulary, antibiogram and consultant-specific pathway.

title: Neonatal HSV infection - suspected or confirmed
summary: Admit to NICU/PICU or neonatal-capable monitored unit; disseminated disease, hepatitis, coagulopathy, shock, seizures or respiratory failure requires intensive care.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit to NICU/PICU or neonatal-capable monitored unit; disseminated disease, hepatitis, coagulopathy, shock, seizures or respiratory failure requires intensive care.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring; q1-2h neuro/perfusion assessment when ill.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitoring: Strict intake/output, daily weight, seizure surveillance, serial liver/coagulation/renal trends; continuous EEG if encephalopathy/seizures.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/ventilation as required; manage apnea and shock promptly.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access: Reliable IV access; central access may be needed for 14-21 days of therapy but should not delay the first dose.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Fluids/diet: Breast milk/formula if safe; isotonic glucose-containing IV fluids when ill/NPO; careful fluid management with hepatitis/SIADH.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Labs: Surface swabs (conjunctivae, mouth/nasopharynx, rectum and lesions) for HSV PCR/culture, blood HSV PCR, CSF cell count/protein/glucose and HSV PCR when safe; CBC, AST/ALT, bilirubin, INR/PTT/fibrinogen, renal function and cultures for bacterial sepsis.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging: MRI brain and EEG for CNS disease; chest/abdominal imaging based on organ involvement. Ophthalmologic examination for eye disease.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Medications/treatments: Start acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h immediately when suspected; adjust interval for gestational age/renal function. Continue 14 days for skin-eye-mouth disease and at least 21 days for CNS/disseminated disease, with repeat CSF HSV PCR near completion for CNS disease. Maintain IV hydration and renal monitoring.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Consults: ID, neonatology/PICU, neurology for CNS disease, ophthalmology for eye involvement, hematology for coagulopathy.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Nursing instructions: Contact precautions for active lesions; monitor IV site, urine output and creatinine; lesion care; document maternal HSV history but do not let absent history reduce suspicion.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassessment/contingency: Review liver/coagulation/renal status daily or more often when ill. Shock, rising transaminases/INR, seizures, apnea or worsening encephalopathy requires immediate PICU and disseminated-HSV management.

treatments.text: Respiratory support: Oxygen/ventilation as required; manage apnea and shock promptly.

Medications/treatments: Start acyclovir 20 mg/kg IV q8h immediately when suspected; adjust interval for gestational age/renal function. Continue 14 days for skin-eye-mouth disease and at least 21 days for CNS/disseminated disease, with repeat CSF HSV PCR near completion for CNS disease. Maintain IV hydration and renal monitoring.

title: Pyloric stenosis
summary: Admit for dehydration/electrolyte correction and surgical management. Keep NPO. Urgent escalation for shock, apnea, severe alkalosis, or inability to obtain access.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for dehydration/electrolyte correction and surgical management. Keep NPO. Urgent escalation for shock, apnea, severe alkalosis, or inability to obtain access.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable; increase frequency for abnormal perfusion, respiratory distress, neurologic change, active resuscitation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Strict intake/output, emesis, daily weight, hydration, glucose and serial electrolytes until corrected.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen and escalating respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygen requirement, ventilation, and fatigue after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Establish IV access when parenteral therapy, fluids, urgent investigations, procedural sedation, or clinical instability is present. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Use oral intake when safe. Select isotonic IV fluids according to hydration, renal/cardiac status, glucose, electrolytes, and ongoing losses. Avoid routine fluid loading when cerebral, cardiac, or renal edema is a concern.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Electrolytes, glucose, urea/creatinine, venous gas; CBC and type/screen when requested by surgery/anesthesia.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Abdominal ultrasound when diagnosis is not already confirmed.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: NPO; isotonic fluid resuscitation when needed, then chloride/potassium repletion guided by urine output and serial electrolytes. Surgery occurs after metabolic correction rather than immediately.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Pediatric surgery and anesthesia.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Document neurologic, respiratory, perfusion, pain, intake/output, and safeguarding observations relevant to the syndrome. Confirm current weight, allergies, medication timing, and escalation parameters.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Recheck electrolytes and gas after fluid correction. Escalate for persistent oliguria, worsening alkalosis, respiratory depression, or shock.

treatments.text: Oxygen and escalating respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygen requirement, ventilation, and fatigue after every intervention. sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable; increase frequency for abnormal perfusion, respiratory distress, neurologic change, active resuscitation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.text: Medications/treatments: Quiet environment and hydration only when clinically depleted. summary: Admit a symptomatic or moderate/large pneumothorax, any patient requiring oxygen or drainage, traumatic or secondary pneumothorax, bilateral disease, or unreliable follow-up. Tension physiology requires immediate emergency decompression and PICU/trauma escalation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit a symptomatic or moderate/large pneumothorax, any patient requiring oxygen or drainage, traumatic or secondary pneumothorax, bilateral disease, or unreliable follow-up. Tension physiology requires immediate emergency decompression and PICU/trauma escalation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous oxygen saturation and cardiorespiratory monitoring when symptomatic, receiving oxygen, after drainage, or when tension physiology is possible. Document chest pain, work of breathing and drain output/air leak.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen for hypoxemia. Avoid positive-pressure ventilation when possible before pleural decompression in tension physiology. Escalate ventilatory support with senior/PICU involvement.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet if stable and no procedure is planned. Keep NPO when sedation, chest-tube insertion or surgery is anticipated.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Routine bloodwork is not required for a small stable spontaneous event. Obtain CBC, gas, electrolytes, type/screen and trauma studies according to severity and procedure needs.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph or point-of-care ultrasound confirms diagnosis when this does not delay emergency decompression. Repeat imaging after intervention and according to clinical change.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Analgesia, oxygen when indicated and pleural drainage according to size, symptoms, etiology and local pathway. Do not delay decompression for imaging when tension pneumothorax is clinically suspected.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Respiratory medicine, surgery/trauma and PICU according to cause and severity.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Notify immediately for increasing distress, falling oxygen saturation, hypotension, tracheal deviation, sudden drain cessation, expanding subcutaneous emphysema or new asymmetry.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate persistent air leak, recurrent pneumothorax, hemodynamic compromise, worsening oxygen need or ventilation requirement.

treatments.text: Give oxygen for hypoxemia. Avoid positive-pressure ventilation when possible before pleural decompression in tension physiology. Escalate ventilatory support with senior/PICU involvement. Regular diet if stable and no procedure is planned. Keep NPO when sedation, chest-tube insertion or surgery is anticipated.

Analgesia, oxygen when indicated and pleural drainage according to size, symptoms, etiology and local pathway. Do not delay decompression for imaging when tension pneumothorax is clinically suspected.

guidance: Current local pneumothorax, trauma and pleural-drain pathways.
contentStatus: Structured PedsFlow reference — local clinical review required

title: Hemoptysis
summary: Admit recurrent, moderate or large-volume hemoptysis; respiratory compromise; anemia; abnormal imaging; coagulopathy; chronic lung disease; or uncertain source. Major bleeding with airway threat requires immediate PICU, anesthesia and respiratory escalation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit recurrent, moderate or large-volume hemoptysis; respiratory compromise; anemia; abnormal imaging; coagulopathy; chronic lung disease; or uncertain source. Major bleeding with airway threat requires immediate PICU, anesthesia and respiratory escalation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory and oxygen monitoring for active bleeding. Quantify blood loss, distinguish hemoptysis from hematemesis/epistaxis and trend perfusion.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Position the suspected bleeding lung down when the side is known and airway protection is threatened. Give oxygen and prepare for controlled airway management with experienced support.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain two IVs for significant or ongoing bleeding. Send type/screen early and prepare blood products when major hemorrhage is possible.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Keep NPO during active/significant bleeding and when bronchoscopy or procedure is likely. Use cautious isotonic resuscitation and blood products according to hemorrhage status.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, coagulation profile, fibrinogen, type/screen, renal/liver profile and targeted infection/autoimmune testing. Blood gas and lactate when unstable.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph initially. CT angiography and bronchoscopy are selected with respiratory, radiology and surgical teams according to stability and suspected source.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Treat the cause and correct clinically significant coagulopathy. Avoid medications that impair hemostasis. Antimicrobials, antifibrinolytics or embolization require syndrome-specific specialist direction.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Respiratory medicine, PICU, ENT if an upper-airway source is possible, interventional radiology and hematology as indicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Record estimated volume and frequency. Have suction and emergency airway equipment available for active major bleeding.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate increasing volume, hypoxemia, fatigue, hemodynamic change, falling hemoglobin or inability to protect the airway.

treatments.text: Position the suspected bleeding lung down when the side is known and airway protection is threatened. Give oxygen and prepare for controlled airway management with experienced support. Keep NPO during active/significant bleeding and when bronchoscopy or procedure is likely. Use cautious isotonic resuscitation and blood products according to hemorrhage status.

Treat the cause and correct clinically significant coagulopathy. Avoid medications that impair hemostasis. Antimicrobials, antifibrinolytics or embolization require syndrome-specific specialist direction.

guidance: Current local pulmonary hemorrhage and major-hemoptysis pathway.

title: Cystic fibrosis pulmonary exacerbation
summary: Admit increased respiratory symptoms with hypoxemia, significant lung-function decline, failure of outpatient therapy, dehydration, hemoptysis, pneumothorax, severe nutritional compromise or need for IV antimicrobials/airway clearance.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit increased respiratory symptoms with hypoxemia, significant lung-function decline, failure of outpatient therapy, dehydration, hemoptysis, pneumothorax, severe nutritional compromise or need for IV antimicrobials/airway clearance.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Oxygen saturation, respiratory effort, sputum burden, weight, intake/output and spirometry when feasible. Monitor antimicrobial toxicity and line complications.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen for hypoxemia. Continue individualized airway-clearance and inhaled therapies with respiratory therapy. Escalate support with the CF/PICU team.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: High-calorie diet, pancreatic enzyme replacement and fat-soluble vitamins as prescribed. Address dehydration, constipation and CF-related diabetes according to the established plan.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Sputum/throat culture, CBC, CRP, electrolytes, renal/liver profile and glucose; additional drug levels and spirometry according to the treatment regimen.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph for severe, focal or atypical deterioration or suspected pneumothorax. CT is not routine for every exacerbation.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Select antimicrobials from current and prior respiratory cultures, allergies and resistance history. Continue airway clearance, bronchodilator therapy when prescribed and chronic CF medications unless contraindicated.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: CF respirology, respiratory therapy, dietitian, pharmacy and endocrinology when CFRD is relevant.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Document airway-clearance sessions, sputum, weight, enzymes with meals and symptoms suggesting drug toxicity.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate hemoptysis, pneumothorax, worsening hypercapnia, respiratory fatigue or failure to improve.

treatments.text: Oxygen for hypoxemia. Continue individualized airway-clearance and inhaled therapies with respiratory therapy. Escalate support with the CF/PICU team. High-calorie diet, pancreatic enzyme replacement and fat-soluble vitamins as prescribed. Address dehydration, constipation and CF-related diabetes according to the established plan.

Select antimicrobials from current and prior respiratory cultures, allergies and resistance history. Continue airway clearance, bronchodilator therapy when prescribed and chronic CF medications unless contraindicated.

guidance: Current Canadian CF-care standards and the patient-specific CF action plan.

title: Bronchiectasis pulmonary exacerbation
summary: Admit hypoxemia, respiratory distress, significant dehydration, hemoptysis, failure of oral treatment, resistant prior organisms, or need for intensive airway clearance/IV therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit hypoxemia, respiratory distress, significant dehydration, hemoptysis, failure of oral treatment, resistant prior organisms, or need for intensive airway clearance/IV therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Oxygen saturation, work of breathing, sputum quantity/quality, fever, hydration and response to airway clearance.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen for hypoxemia. Continue or intensify airway-clearance techniques with respiratory therapy. Use bronchodilator therapy when bronchospasm is present or part of the usual plan.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Encourage hydration and nutrition. Use isotonic IV fluid only when oral intake is inadequate or dehydration is documented.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Sputum culture, CBC, CRP and renal/liver profile for moderate/severe disease or IV therapy.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph for focal findings, severe deterioration or complications. CT is not routine during every exacerbation.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Choose antimicrobials using prior cultures and current local guidance; include Pseudomonas coverage only when epidemiology or prior cultures support it. Continue airway clearance.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Respiratory medicine, physiotherapy/RT and infectious diseases for resistant or unusual organisms.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Record airway-clearance sessions, sputum, oxygen requirement and medication tolerance.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate increasing oxygen need, major hemoptysis, respiratory fatigue, hypercapnia or failure to improve.

treatments.text: Oxygen for hypoxemia. Continue or intensify airway-clearance techniques with respiratory therapy. Use bronchodilator therapy when bronchospasm is present or part of the usual plan. Encourage hydration and nutrition. Use isotonic IV fluid only when oral intake is inadequate or dehydration is documented.
Choose antimicrobials using prior cultures and current local guidance; include Pseudomonas coverage only when epidemiology or prior cultures support it. Continue airway clearance.

guidance: Current pediatric bronchiectasis and local antimicrobial pathways.

title: Obstructive sleep apnea with hypoxemia
summary: Admit persistent nocturnal hypoxemia, hypercapnia, severe obstruction, cardiorespiratory consequences, postoperative airway concern, inability to use prescribed support or unsafe home monitoring.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit persistent nocturnal hypoxemia, hypercapnia, severe obstruction, cardiorespiratory consequences, postoperative airway concern, inability to use prescribed support or unsafe home monitoring.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous oxygen saturation during sleep and cardiorespiratory monitoring when severe. Document obstruction, position, arousals, CO2 when available and response to support.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Positioning and prescribed CPAP/BiPAP are preferred when tolerated. Oxygen alone may mask hypoventilation and should be used with appropriate monitoring and specialist direction.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access is not routinely required unless the child is medically unstable, dehydrated or undergoing a procedure.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet when awake and safe. Observe aspiration risk and keep NPO when urgent airway surgery or sedation is likely.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Blood gas or capillary CO2 when hypoventilation is suspected; targeted CBC, electrolytes and cardiopulmonary testing according to severity.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging is not routine. Echocardiography or airway imaging is selected for pulmonary hypertension, anatomic obstruction or syndromic concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Use the patient's established non-invasive ventilation settings when available. Avoid sedating medications that worsen obstruction unless monitored and specifically indicated.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: ENT, respiratory/sleep medicine and PICU/anesthesia for severe obstruction or support failure.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Document events during sleep, device tolerance, mask leak, oxygen and CO2 trend. Maintain airway emergency readiness.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate recurrent severe desaturation, rising CO2, reduced arousability, bradycardia, inability to tolerate support or postoperative airway deterioration.

treatments.text: Positioning and prescribed CPAP/BiPAP are preferred when tolerated. Oxygen alone may mask hypoventilation and should be used with appropriate monitoring and specialist direction. Regular diet when awake and safe. Observe aspiration risk and keep NPO when urgent airway surgery or sedation is likely.
Use the patient's established non-invasive ventilation settings when available. Avoid sedating medications that worsen obstruction unless monitored and specifically indicated.

guidance: Current local pediatric sleep-disordered breathing and perioperative airway pathways.

title: Home ventilation or BiPAP failure
summary: Admit device-dependent children with increased support needs, repeated alarms, secretion burden, suspected infection, equipment failure, caregiver inability to safely provide support or abnormal gas exchange.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit device-dependent children with increased support needs, repeated alarms, secretion burden, suspected infection, equipment failure, caregiver inability to safely provide support or abnormal gas exchange.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory and oxygen monitoring. Compare current settings and alarms with the baseline care plan; document secretions, interface leak and work of breathing.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Use the child's backup device/settings when safe and verified. Provide airway clearance and suction. Escalate to hospital non-invasive or invasive ventilation with PICU/RT support.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Continue usual enteral feeds only when respiratory status and aspiration risk permit. Use IV hydration cautiously if feeds are withheld.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Blood gas, CBC, electrolytes and infection testing according to presentation. Check device data and obtain respiratory cultures when indicated.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph for respiratory deterioration; additional imaging according to suspected complication.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Treat the cause rather than only increasing settings. Verify equipment, circuit, humidification, mask/tracheostomy position and medications. Antimicrobials follow the syndrome and prior cultures.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: PICU, respiratory therapy, complex care/home ventilation team and biomedical equipment support.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Keep the baseline emergency plan, spare interface/tracheostomy equipment and resuscitation equipment at bedside.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate rising CO2, recurrent apnea, inability to ventilate, increasing oxygen need, altered mental status or equipment failure without a safe backup.

treatments.text: Use the child's backup device/settings when safe and verified. Provide airway clearance and suction. Escalate to hospital non-invasive or invasive ventilation with PICU/RT support. Continue usual enteral feeds only when respiratory status and aspiration risk permit. Use IV hydration cautiously if feeds are withheld.
Treat the cause rather than only increasing settings. Verify equipment, circuit, humidification, mask/tracheostomy position and medications. Antimicrobials follow the syndrome and prior cultures.

guidance: Patient-specific home ventilation plan and current local complex-care pathway.

title: Fever of unknown origin or prolonged fever
summary: Admit hemodynamic instability, weight loss/dehydration, organ dysfunction, concerning examination, immunocompromise, inability to complete evaluation safely as outpatient or high-risk social circumstances.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit hemodynamic instability, weight loss/dehydration, organ dysfunction, concerning examination, immunocompromise, inability to complete evaluation safely as outpatient or high-risk social circumstances.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Fever curve, weight, hydration, rash, lymph nodes, joints, cardiac/respiratory findings and repeated targeted examinations.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access when unstable, dehydrated or requiring serial investigations/treatment. Avoid repeated low-value blood draws without a diagnostic plan.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet and oral hydration when safe. Correct documented dehydration.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC/differential, inflammatory markers, renal/liver profile, urinalysis/culture and blood cultures according to clinical pattern. Add targeted infectious, inflammatory, malignant and immunologic tests after history/examination review.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging must be hypothesis-driven. Chest radiograph, ultrasound, echocardiography, MRI or whole-body imaging should follow focused findings and consultant input.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Avoid empiric broad-spectrum antimicrobials in a stable child without a defined indication. Treat immediately when sepsis, endocarditis, meningitis or another high-risk syndrome is suspected.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Infectious diseases; rheumatology, hematology/oncology, cardiology or other services according to the evolving differential.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Maintain an accurate fever and specimen timeline. Document travel, exposures, medications, animals, immunization and prior antimicrobial use.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate new shock, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, cytopenias, coagulopathy, cardiac findings or rapidly progressive inflammation.

treatments.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention. Regular diet and oral hydration when safe. Correct documented dehydration.
Avoid empiric broad-spectrum antimicrobials in a stable child without a defined indication. Treat immediately when sepsis, endocarditis, meningitis or another high-risk syndrome is suspected.

guidance: Current CPS/TREKK resources and specialist-directed prolonged-fever evaluation.

title: Central line-associated bloodstream infection
summary: Admit suspected line infection with fever, rigors, hemodynamic change, immunocompromise, positive culture or need for IV therapy. Septic shock requires immediate resuscitation and source-control planning.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit suspected line infection with fever, rigors, hemodynamic change, immunocompromise, positive culture or need for IV therapy. Septic shock requires immediate resuscitation and source-control planning.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring when unstable. Inspect catheter sites and document perfusion, line function, rigors and infusion-related symptoms.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen and ventilation support according to sepsis physiology.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain peripheral and line cultures from each lumen before antibiotics when this will not delay treatment. Establish alternate access when the line is unsafe or source control is anticipated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Use isotonic sepsis resuscitation with frequent reassessment. Continue nutrition when stable and procedures are not imminent.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Paired blood cultures, CBC, renal/liver profile, lactate when unstable and organism/source-specific tests. Repeat cultures according to organism and clearance plan.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Ultrasound for thrombosis or tunnel infection; echocardiography for persistent bacteremia or endocarditis concern; other imaging by metastatic focus.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Start empiric therapy according to host, line type, unit flora and prior organisms. Remove or salvage the catheter only according to organism, stability, complications and ID/line-team guidance.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Infectious diseases, oncology/complex care, vascular access team and surgery/interventional radiology when removal is required.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Do not use the affected line unless the clinical plan allows it. Label culture source/lumen accurately and document antimicrobial timing.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate shock, persistent bacteremia, tunnel infection, thrombosis, endocarditis, metastatic infection or inability to obtain source control.

treatments.text: Oxygen and ventilation support according to sepsis physiology. Use isotonic sepsis resuscitation with frequent reassessment. Continue nutrition when stable and procedures are not imminent.
Start empiric therapy according to host, line type, unit flora and prior organisms. Remove or salvage the catheter only according to organism, stability, complications and ID/line-team guidance.

guidance: Current local CLABSI, vascular-access and antimicrobial-stewardship pathways.

title: Infective endocarditis
summary: Admit all suspected pediatric infective endocarditis. Escalate heart failure, embolic phenomena, conduction abnormality, prosthetic material infection or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit all suspected pediatric infective endocarditis. Escalate heart failure, embolic phenomena, conduction abnormality, prosthetic material infection or hemodynamic instability.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Cardiorespiratory monitoring, fever curve, perfusion, new murmur, neurologic examination, skin/eye findings and embolic symptoms.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen and respiratory support for heart failure or septic complications.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain multiple appropriately timed blood-culture sets before antimicrobials when the child is stable. Secure reliable IV access without delaying sepsis therapy.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet when stable. Restrict or manage fluids only according to heart failure and renal status.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Multiple blood cultures, CBC, CRP/ESR, renal/liver profile, urinalysis and organism-specific testing. Trend cultures until clearance.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Echocardiography is required. Additional neuro, chest, abdominal or vascular imaging is guided by embolic or metastatic symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Begin empiric therapy after cultures using valve status, prosthetic material, host factors and local guidance. Narrow to organism and susceptibility. Duration and surgical indications are specialist-directed.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Cardiology, infectious diseases, cardiac surgery and PICU according to severity.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Record every culture time/source, antimicrobial dose time, murmur and neurologic change.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate acute heart failure, arrhythmia/conduction change, stroke symptoms, persistent bacteremia, enlarging vegetation or valve dysfunction.

treatments.text: Oxygen and respiratory support for heart failure or septic complications. Regular diet when stable. Restrict or manage fluids only according to heart failure and renal status.

Begin empiric therapy after cultures using valve status, prosthetic material, host factors and local guidance. Narrow to organism and susceptibility. Duration and surgical indications are specialist-directed.

guidance: Current Canadian/local infective-endocarditis pathway.

title: Complicated bacterial sinusitis
summary: Admit orbital, intracranial or osseous complications; toxic appearance; severe headache/neurologic features; inability to tolerate oral therapy; immunocompromise; or failure of appropriate outpatient treatment.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit orbital, intracranial or osseous complications; toxic appearance; severe headache/neurologic features; inability to tolerate oral therapy; immunocompromise; or failure of appropriate outpatient treatment.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Fever, pain, eye examination, cranial nerves, neurologic status, hydration and response to therapy.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access for parenteral antimicrobials, hydration and contrast imaging when indicated.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet when safe. Keep NPO when surgery or sedation is likely.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, CRP, blood cultures when febrile/toxic and targeted cultures from operative drainage rather than superficial nasal swabs.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI for orbital/intracranial complications; avoid routine imaging for uncomplicated sinusitis.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Use IV therapy covering expected sinus organisms and modify for intracranial extension, MRSA risk or prior cultures. Source control is required for selected abscesses or deterioration.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: ENT; ophthalmology for orbital disease; neurosurgery/neurology and ID for intracranial complications.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Frequent eye and neurologic checks. Document pain, vision, proptosis and extraocular movement.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate visual change, ophthalmoplegia, altered mental status, focal deficit, seizure, meningismus or failure to improve.

treatments.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention. Regular diet when safe. Keep NPO when surgery or sedation is likely.
Use IV therapy covering expected sinus organisms and modify for intracranial extension, MRSA risk or prior cultures. Source control is required for selected abscesses or deterioration.

title: Peritonsillar abscess
summary: Admit airway concern, dehydration, inability to swallow secretions, severe pain, failed outpatient therapy, immunocompromise or need for operative drainage.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit airway concern, dehydration, inability to swallow secretions, severe pain, failed outpatient therapy, immunocompromise or need for operative drainage.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Airway, voice, drooling, hydration, neck movement, fever and pain.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Keep the child calm and upright. Give oxygen if hypoxemic. Prepare for difficult-airway support when obstruction is concerning.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: NPO until airway and drainage plan are established. Use isotonic hydration for poor intake.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Routine labs are not mandatory in a stable classic presentation. CBC, CRP and blood cultures are selected for toxic or complicated disease.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging is not routine when examination is diagnostic. Ultrasound or contrast CT is used for atypical, deep-neck or complication concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Analgesia and antimicrobial therapy covering streptococci and oral anaerobes. Drainage strategy is determined by ENT and patient cooperation/severity.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: ENT and anesthesia when drainage or airway intervention is needed.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Keep suction available. Notify for increasing drooling, trismus, stridor, neck swelling or inability to handle secretions.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate airway compromise, deep-neck spread, mediastinal symptoms, sepsis or failure to improve after drainage/therapy.

treatments.text: Keep the child calm and upright. Give oxygen if hypoxemic. Prepare for difficult-airway support when obstruction is concerning. NPO until airway and drainage plan are established. Use isotonic hydration for poor intake.
Analgesia and antimicrobial therapy covering streptococci and oral anaerobes. Drainage strategy is determined by ENT and patient cooperation/severity.

title: Dental or facial infection
summary: Admit airway concern, rapidly spreading facial/neck infection, systemic toxicity, dehydration, orbital involvement, immunocompromise or inability to obtain urgent dental source control.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit airway concern, rapidly spreading facial/neck infection, systemic toxicity, dehydration, orbital involvement, immunocompromise or inability to obtain urgent dental source control.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Airway, mouth opening, floor of mouth, swallowing, hydration, fever, eye examination and progression of swelling.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Keep upright and avoid agitation when floor-of-mouth or deep-neck swelling threatens the airway. Escalate early to anesthesia/ENT.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Soft diet when safe. Keep NPO if drainage/extraction or airway intervention is planned.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, CRP and blood cultures for toxic/complicated disease. Obtain operative cultures from drainage when clinically useful.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging is not routine for a localized dental abscess. Contrast CT is considered for deep-space spread, orbital involvement, osteomyelitis or airway concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Analgesia and antimicrobial therapy covering oral streptococci and anaerobes. Definitive dental extraction or drainage is essential source control.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Dentistry/oral-maxillofacial surgery; ENT/anesthesia for deep-neck or airway involvement.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Frequent airway and swelling checks. Maintain oral care and document ability to swallow.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate tongue/floor-of-mouth elevation, drooling, voice change, stridor, orbital findings, sepsis or progressive swelling.

treatments.text: Keep upright and avoid agitation when floor-of-mouth or deep-neck swelling threatens the airway. Escalate early to anesthesia/ENT. Soft diet when safe. Keep NPO if drainage/extraction or airway intervention is planned.

title: Necrotizing soft tissue infection
summary: Immediate surgical and PICU emergency. Admit any suspected case with severe pain, rapidly progressive swelling, bullae, skin anesthesia, crepitus, shock or systemic toxicity.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Immediate surgical and PICU emergency. Admit any suspected case with severe pain, rapidly progressive swelling, bullae, skin anesthesia, crepitus, shock or systemic toxicity.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous hemodynamic monitoring, urine output, pain, skin progression and limb perfusion. Mark the edge/time of visible changes.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Provide oxygen and organ support according to sepsis/shock. Prepare for repeated anesthesia and ventilation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain two large-bore IVs or IV/IO access. Draw cultures and critical labs without delaying surgery or antimicrobials.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: NPO. Use reassessment-guided isotonic resuscitation and blood products as clinically indicated.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, CK, lactate, gas, coagulation, fibrinogen, blood cultures and operative tissue cultures.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging must not delay operative exploration when clinical suspicion is high. CT/MRI may define extent only in stable uncertain cases.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Immediate broad empiric therapy covering streptococci, staphylococci, Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes, plus toxin-suppressing therapy according to local protocol. Urgent surgical debridement is definitive.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Surgery, PICU, infectious diseases, anesthesia and transfusion medicine.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Frequent skin/perfusion checks; prepare for urgent theatre and repeated debridement.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate any delay to source control, rising lactate, shock, coagulopathy, compartment syndrome or organ failure.

treatments.text: Provide oxygen and organ support according to sepsis/shock. Prepare for repeated anesthesia and ventilation. NPO. Use reassessment-guided isotonic resuscitation and blood products as clinically indicated.

title: Clostridioides difficile colitis
summary: Admit severe dehydration, ileus, toxic megacolon concern, significant abdominal pain/distension, bloody stool, renal injury, immunocompromise or inability to maintain oral therapy.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit severe dehydration, ileus, toxic megacolon concern, significant abdominal pain/distension, bloody stool, renal injury, immunocompromise or inability to maintain oral therapy.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Stool frequency, abdominal examination, hydration, urine output, fever and signs of ileus or systemic toxicity.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Enteral hydration/nutrition when tolerated. Avoid unnecessary bowel rest unless ileus or surgery requires it.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, albumin, lactate when severe and stool testing only in patients with compatible diarrhea. Avoid testing formed stool.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Abdominal radiograph or CT only for severe pain, distension, ileus, perforation or toxic megacolon concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Stop unnecessary inciting antimicrobials and acid suppression when appropriate. Use age/severity-specific therapy from the current local pathway. Avoid antimotility agents.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Infectious diseases, gastroenterology and surgery for fulminant disease or megacolon.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Contact precautions, soap-and-water hand hygiene and accurate stool/output documentation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate ileus, increasing distension, peritonism, shock, rising lactate or renal deterioration.

title: Thyroid storm
summary: PICU admission for suspected thyroid storm with fever, marked tachycardia, heart failure, delirium, vomiting/diarrhea or hepatic dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: PICU admission for suspected thyroid storm with fever, marked tachycardia, heart failure, delirium, vomiting/diarrhea or hepatic dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, temperature, neurologic status, perfusion, urine output and heart-failure assessment.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen and ventilatory support according to cardiopulmonary status. Avoid excessive stimulation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain reliable IV access and a second line when unstable.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Use cautious isotonic fluids with frequent reassessment because heart failure may coexist. Treat hypoglycemia and hyperthermia.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: TSH, free T4/T3, CBC, electrolytes, glucose, renal/liver profile, gas/lactate, cultures and trigger-specific testing.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: ECG and echocardiography when heart failure/arrhythmia is suspected; chest imaging according to respiratory findings.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Treatment sequence and agents must follow urgent endocrinology/PICU guidance: control adrenergic symptoms, inhibit hormone synthesis/release, give corticosteroid when indicated and treat the trigger.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Endocrinology, PICU, cardiology and infectious diseases according to trigger.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Continuous rhythm and temperature monitoring. Avoid aspirin for fever because it can increase free thyroid hormone.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate arrhythmia, shock, heart failure, hyperthermia, seizure, hepatic failure or worsening delirium.

treatments.text: Oxygen and ventilatory support according to cardiopulmonary status. Avoid excessive stimulation. Use cautious isotonic fluids with frequent reassessment because heart failure may coexist. Treat hypoglycemia and hyperthermia.

title: Severe hypothyroidism or myxedema
summary: Admit severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, altered mental status, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia or cardiovascular instability; PICU for organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, altered mental status, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia or cardiovascular instability; PICU for organ dysfunction.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, temperature, neurologic status, glucose, sodium and ventilation.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Support oxygenation/ventilation cautiously. Avoid sedatives when possible because respiratory depression may be profound.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Correct hypoglycemia and sodium carefully. Rewarm gradually and avoid aggressive peripheral warming in shock.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: TSH, free T4, glucose, electrolytes, cortisol before steroid when feasible, CBC, renal/liver profile, gas and infection testing.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: ECG, chest radiograph and echocardiography according to bradycardia, effusion or heart-failure findings.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Thyroid replacement route and loading strategy require endocrinology/PICU direction. Give stress-dose corticosteroid when adrenal insufficiency has not been excluded and treat the precipitating illness.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Endocrinology and PICU; cardiology for significant cardiac involvement.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Frequent temperature, glucose, sodium, rhythm and mental-status checks.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate hypoventilation, bradyarrhythmia, hypotension, worsening hyponatremia, seizure or coma.

treatments.text: Support oxygenation/ventilation cautiously. Avoid sedatives when possible because respiratory depression may be profound. Correct hypoglycemia and sodium carefully. Rewarm gradually and avoid aggressive peripheral warming in shock.

title: Diabetes insipidus
summary: Admit hypernatremia, dehydration, altered mental status, inability to access water, postoperative/neurosurgical DI, uncertain diagnosis or need for monitored desmopressin/fluid adjustment.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit hypernatremia, dehydration, altered mental status, inability to access water, postoperative/neurosurgical DI, uncertain diagnosis or need for monitored desmopressin/fluid adjustment.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Strict hourly intake/output when unstable, urine specific gravity/osmolality, serial weight, neurologic status and sodium trend.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access for hypernatremia, dehydration or inability to drink. Avoid unmonitored large fluid changes.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Allow free access to water when awake and safe unless a controlled correction plan is required. Replace deficits and ongoing urine losses under endocrine guidance.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Serial sodium, glucose, serum/urine osmolality, urine specific gravity, renal profile and cause-specific pituitary testing.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Brain/pituitary MRI is selected after stabilization and endocrine/neurosurgical assessment; postoperative imaging depends on context.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Desmopressin is used only after confirming the clinical pattern and with close sodium/fluid monitoring. Treat adrenal or other pituitary deficiencies when present.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Endocrinology; neurosurgery/oncology according to cause; PICU for severe hypernatremia or neurologic change.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Measure every intake and output. Notify before giving desmopressin if urine output has fallen or sodium is decreasing unexpectedly.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate rapid sodium change, seizure, altered mental status, shock, oliguria after desmopressin or inability to match losses.

treatments.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention. sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit symptomatic or marked hypercalcemia, dehydration, AKI, arrhythmia, pancreatitis, altered mental status, suspected malignancy or inability to ensure close follow-up.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Cardiac rhythm for significant elevation, neurologic status, hydration, urine output and symptoms of nephrolithiasis/pancreatitis.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Use isotonic hydration with careful reassessment. Avoid calcium/vitamin D supplements and medications that worsen hypercalcemia.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Repeat total and ionized calcium, albumin, phosphate, magnesium, creatinine, PTH, vitamin D metabolites, urine calcium and cause-specific malignant/endocrine studies.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: ECG; renal ultrasound for stones/nephrocalcinosis; imaging directed by suspected malignancy, granulomatous disease or endocrine cause.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Treatment beyond hydration depends on severity and cause and may include calcitonin, bisphosphonate or dialysis under endocrine/nephrology/oncology direction.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Endocrinology and nephrology; oncology when malignancy is possible.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Strict intake/output and cardiac monitoring when severe. Avoid prolonged immobilization when safe mobilization is possible.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate arrhythmia, AKI/oliguria, pancreatitis, seizure, severe hypertension or worsening mental status.

treatments.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention. sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Cardiac monitoring during significant IV replacement and for arrhythmia risk; neurologic status, reflexes and serial electrolytes.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain secure IV access for symptomatic or severe deficiency. Use controlled infusion through an appropriate line.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Continue oral intake when safe. Replace ongoing GI losses and review medications causing renal magnesium wasting.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Magnesium, potassium, calcium, phosphate, renal function, ECG and urine studies when renal wasting is suspected.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging is not routinely required.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Use oral replacement for stable mild deficiency and IV replacement for severe/symptomatic disease according to the current local electrolyte protocol. Correct associated potassium/calcium abnormalities.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Endocrinology/nephrology for persistent or renal-wasting cases; pharmacy for IV administration.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Monitor line site, rhythm, blood pressure and serial magnesium. Avoid rapid infusion.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate arrhythmia, seizure, hypotension, respiratory depression or recurrent severe deficiency.

treatments.text: Give oxygen and escalate respiratory support only when clinically indicated. Reassess work of breathing, oxygenation and ventilation after every intervention. Continue oral intake when safe. Replace ongoing GI losses and review medications causing renal magnesium wasting.

title: Hyperammonemia or suspected metabolic decompensation
summary: PICU/metabolic emergency for elevated ammonia with vomiting, lethargy, encephalopathy, respiratory alkalosis, seizure or known inborn error of metabolism.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: PICU/metabolic emergency for elevated ammonia with vomiting, lethargy, encephalopathy, respiratory alkalosis, seizure or known inborn error of metabolism.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Frequent neurologic checks, continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, strict intake/output, glucose and serial ammonia using correct specimen handling.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Protect airway and ventilate when consciousness declines. Avoid delays that allow progressive cerebral edema.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain two IVs/IO and contact the metabolic team immediately. Preserve access for high-glucose therapy, scavengers or dialysis.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Stop protein temporarily only under metabolic guidance. Prevent catabolism with high-calorie glucose/lipid therapy and treat hypoglycemia. Avoid excessive fluid.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Urgent ammonia, gas, glucose, electrolytes, lactate, ketones, liver profile, coagulation and metabolic specimens collected before therapy when this does not delay treatment.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Neuroimaging only when clinically required and safe; it must not delay ammonia-lowering treatment.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Use the patient's emergency metabolic protocol. Nitrogen scavengers, arginine/citrulline, carglumic acid or dialysis are diagnosis-specific and specialist-directed.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Metabolic genetics, PICU, nephrology/dialysis and pharmacy immediately.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Use ammonia-specific collection/transport instructions. Minimize fasting and document all caloric intake.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate rising ammonia, worsening GCS, seizure, cerebral edema, respiratory alkalosis progressing to failure or inability to start dialysis rapidly.

treatments.text: Protect airway and ventilate when consciousness declines. Avoid delays that allow progressive cerebral edema. Stop protein temporarily only under metabolic guidance. Prevent catabolism with high-calorie glucose/lipid therapy and treat hypoglycemia. Avoid excessive fluid.

title: Mediastinal mass with airway or cardiovascular risk
summary: Admit all symptomatic or high-risk mediastinal masses. PICU/anesthesia emergency for orthopnea, stridor, superior vena cava obstruction, syncope, pericardial effusion or inability to lie flat.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit all symptomatic or high-risk mediastinal masses. PICU/anesthesia emergency for orthopnea, stridor, superior vena cava obstruction, syncope, pericardial effusion or inability to lie flat.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring in the position of comfort. Document ability to lie flat, work of breathing, facial/upper-body swelling and perfusion.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Avoid sedation, paralysis and supine positioning until a multidisciplinary airway plan exists. Provide oxygen and preserve spontaneous ventilation.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access should be obtained while upright and without distress; avoid delaying stabilization. Consider lower-extremity access when SVC obstruction is present.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Keep NPO when biopsy/procedure is anticipated. Use cautious fluids because cardiac compression/effusion may coexist.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, blood film, tumor lysis studies, renal/liver profile, LDH, uric acid, coagulation and type/screen. Avoid procedures that require unsafe positioning.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Chest radiograph and contrast CT only when the child can tolerate the position; echocardiography for cardiac/vascular compression or effusion.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Do not start corticosteroids or chemotherapy before diagnostic planning unless life-threatening compromise requires it and oncology directs therapy, because treatment can alter tissue diagnosis.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Oncology, anesthesia, PICU, respiratory medicine, cardiology and surgery/interventional radiology.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Maintain the child's position of comfort and emergency airway plan at bedside. Avoid unplanned sedating medication.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate inability to lie flat, stridor, syncope, hypotension, new upper-body edema, worsening effusion or respiratory fatigue.

treatments.text: Avoid sedation, paralysis and supine positioning until a multidisciplinary airway plan exists. Provide oxygen and preserve spontaneous ventilation. Keep NPO when biopsy/procedure is anticipated. Use cautious fluids because cardiac compression/effusion may coexist.

summary: Admit inability to maintain hydration/nutrition, uncontrolled pain, febrile neutropenia, bleeding, airway concern or need for IV analgesia/antimicrobials.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit inability to maintain hydration/nutrition, uncontrolled pain, febrile neutropenia, bleeding, airway concern or need for IV analgesia/antimicrobials.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Pain, oral examination, hydration, intake/output, weight, fever and airway/secretions.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support is rarely required, but escalating oral/pharyngeal edema or secretions require urgent airway assessment.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Obtain IV access for significant illness, parenteral therapy, urgent investigations, procedural care or instability. Consider a second IV/IO during resuscitation.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Use tolerated cool/soft intake, enteral nutrition when feasible and IV hydration when necessary. Avoid irritating foods and alcohol-containing mouth products.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC/differential, electrolytes, renal/liver profile, cultures when febrile and viral/fungal testing for selected lesions.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging only for deep infection, airway complication or another focal concern.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Multimodal analgesia, meticulous oral care and cause-specific antiviral/antifungal/antibacterial therapy when indicated. Avoid topical agents with aspiration/toxicity risk unless supported by the local pathway.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Oncology, pain service, dietitian, dentistry/oral medicine and infectious diseases when complicated.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Scheduled oral care, pain scoring, intake/output and bleeding assessment. Use neutropenic precautions according to the oncology plan.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate airway symptoms, inability to handle secretions, shock, febrile neutropenia, uncontrolled bleeding or progressive renal/electrolyte abnormalities.

treatments.text: Respiratory support is rarely required, but escalating oral/pharyngeal edema or secretions require urgent airway assessment. title: Catheter-associated thrombosis
summary: Admit symptomatic extensive thrombosis, superior vena cava symptoms, pulmonary embolism concern, threatened access, infection, significant bleeding risk or need to initiate monitored anticoagulation.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit symptomatic extensive thrombosis, superior vena cava symptoms, pulmonary embolism concern, threatened access, infection, significant bleeding risk or need to initiate monitored anticoagulation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Limb/neck swelling, perfusion, pain, line function, respiratory symptoms and bleeding surveillance.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Oxygen and cardiopulmonary support if pulmonary embolism or SVC compromise is suspected.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: Use alternative access when the catheter is nonfunctional or unsafe. Do not remove a line automatically before hematology/line-team planning.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet unless a procedure is planned. Maintain hydration without unnecessary fluid loading.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC, coagulation profile, renal/liver function, type/screen and anticoagulation baseline tests. Blood cultures when infection is possible.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Doppler ultrasound is first-line for accessible venous thrombosis; CT/MR venography or pulmonary imaging is selected by location/symptoms.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Anticoagulation choice, intensity and duration depend on location, symptoms, catheter need, bleeding risk and oncology status. Thrombolysis is reserved for selected limb-/life-threatening cases.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Hematology, oncology/complex care, vascular access and interventional radiology/surgery when required.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Measure and document swelling/perfusion, line patency and bleeding. Avoid unnecessary line manipulation.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate respiratory compromise, SVC syndrome, threatened limb, intracranial extension, major bleeding or progressive thrombosis.

treatments.text: Oxygen and cardiopulmonary support if pulmonary embolism or SVC compromise is suspected. Regular diet unless a procedure is planned. Maintain hydration without unnecessary fluid loading.
Anticoagulation choice, intensity and duration depend on location, symptoms, catheter need, bleeding risk and oncology status. Thrombolysis is reserved for selected limb-/life-threatening cases.

guidance: Current pediatric VTE and central-line thrombosis pathway.

title: Aplastic anemia or marrow failure
summary: Admit severe cytopenias with fever, bleeding, symptomatic anemia, hemodynamic compromise or inability to ensure urgent hematology follow-up.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit severe cytopenias with fever, bleeding, symptomatic anemia, hemodynamic compromise or inability to ensure urgent hematology follow-up.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q4h when stable. Increase frequency or use continuous monitoring for hemodynamic instability, respiratory compromise, neurologic change, active resuscitation, procedural sedation, or rapidly evolving disease.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Fever, bleeding, cardiorespiratory symptoms, perfusion and infection surveillance.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Respiratory support according to anemia, infection or bleeding complications.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access for unstable patients, transfusion or antimicrobial therapy; minimize invasive procedures when platelets/neutrophils are very low.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Regular diet with neutropenic food policy only if required by the local hematology program. Maintain hydration.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: CBC/reticulocytes, blood film, type/screen, renal/liver profile, viral testing and marrow-failure workup directed by hematology.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: Imaging is symptom-directed. Avoid routine radiation without a defined question.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Treat fever as a hematology emergency according to neutropenia status. Transfuse based on symptoms, bleeding and specialist thresholds. Avoid unnecessary blood products before transplant planning.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Hematology and transplant service; infectious diseases for complex infection.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Bleeding and infection precautions. Avoid rectal temperatures, IM injections and unnecessary procedures when counts are severely low.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Escalate fever/sepsis, active bleeding, chest pain, syncope, rapidly falling counts or transfusion reaction.

treatments.text: Respiratory support according to anemia, infection or bleeding complications. Regular diet with neutropenic food policy only if required by the local hematology program. Maintain hydration.
Treat fever as a hematology emergency according to neutropenia status. Transfuse based on symptoms, bleeding and specialist thresholds. Avoid unnecessary blood products before transplant planning.
