title: Cannabis hyperemesis syndrome (CHS)
summary: Consider CHS in an adolescent with recurrent/cyclic vomiting, abdominal pain, chronic frequent cannabis exposure and temporary relief with hot showers. Exclude pregnancy, obstruction/surgical abdomen, DKA, pancreatitis/hepatitis, intracranial disease, toxic ingestion and other dangerous causes.

sections.label: Admission / disposition
sections.text: Admit for ongoing vomiting with dehydration/electrolyte abnormality, inability to tolerate oral intake, uncontrolled pain, diagnostic uncertainty, significant medication adverse effects or unsafe mental-health/substance-use disposition. PICU for shock, severe electrolyte disturbance, dysrhythmia/QT prolongation, altered mental status, respiratory depression or need for high-risk sedation.

sections.label: Vitals
sections.text: Vitals q2–4h when stable; increase frequency during active resuscitation, sedating rescue medication or significant electrolyte/QT abnormality.

sections.label: Monitoring
sections.text: Track vomiting frequency, pain, hydration, intake/output, mental status and response/adverse effects after each medication. Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring for significant QT risk, electrolyte abnormality, sedating rescue therapy or instability.

sections.label: Respiratory support
sections.text: Room air if stable. Provide oxygen/ventilatory support for medication-related sedation or another cause of respiratory compromise; avoid casual stacking of sedatives.

sections.label: IV access
sections.text: IV access for dehydration, electrolyte replacement, inability to tolerate oral therapy or monitored rescue medication.

sections.label: Fluids / diet
sections.text: Oral rehydration when tolerated; isotonic IV fluids for dehydration and targeted potassium/magnesium correction. Permit a supervised warm shower only when safe; avoid burns and prolonged unsupervised exposure.

sections.label: Labs
sections.text: Check glucose, electrolytes, bicarbonate, creatinine, potassium and magnesium. Obtain pregnancy testing when relevant. Add liver tests/lipase, urinalysis, toxicology and other investigations according to the differential. Obtain ECG before dopamine antagonists or when dehydrated, hypokalemic/hypomagnesemic, taking QT-active drugs or receiving more than one QT-prolonging agent.

sections.label: Imaging
sections.text: No CHS-specific imaging. Use ultrasound or other imaging when surgical, gynecologic, obstructive or alternate pathology remains possible.

sections.label: Medications / treatment
sections.text: Use a stepwise plan rather than ordering multiple antiemetics simultaneously. 1) Rehydrate and correct potassium/magnesium. 2) Trial ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg PO/IV (max 8 mg). 3) Add topical capsaicin 0.025%–0.075% as a thin layer to abdomen/posterior arms with gloves; avoid eyes, mucosa and damaged skin. 4) If ondansetron clearly fails, reconsider the diagnosis and select ONE monitored rescue agent using the local CHS pathway: haloperidol 0.05 mg/kg (max 2 mg), droperidol 0.05 mg/kg (max 2.5 mg), or lorazepam 0.025–0.05 mg/kg IV once (max 2 mg). Do not casually combine rescue agents. Prior haloperidol-associated dystonia is a strong reason to avoid haloperidol and generally avoid/cautiously review droperidol, metoclopramide and prochlorperazine. If dystonia occurs, stop the causative drug and give diphenhydramine 1 mg/kg IV/IM (max 50 mg) with monitoring. Complete cannabis cessation is the definitive treatment; do not discharge on haloperidol.

sections.label: Consults
sections.text: Adolescent medicine/addiction or mental-health support for cessation planning; pharmacy for QT-active, dopamine-antagonist or sedating rescue therapy; PICU for instability; GI when diagnosis remains uncertain or episodes persist despite abstinence.

sections.label: Nursing / RT instructions
sections.text: Record emesis, intake/output, medication response, sedation/EPS, QT/ECG status when monitored, and skin response to capsaicin. Use gloves for capsaicin and prevent eye/mucosal exposure. Provide nonjudgmental cannabis-use counselling and confidentiality appropriate to age and law.

sections.label: Reassessment / contingency
sections.text: Reassess 30–60 minutes after each treatment step. Escalate for persistent hypotension, worsening acidosis, significant QT prolongation/dysrhythmia, severe electrolyte abnormality, respiratory depression, dystonia, bilious/bloody emesis, peritonism, pregnancy complication or failure to improve. Discharge only when oral intake and electrolytes are safe, dangerous alternatives are excluded, and cessation/follow-up planning is documented.

treatments.text: Rehydrate, correct potassium/magnesium, permit a safe supervised warm shower if desired, and counsel that complete cannabis cessation is definitive treatment.
Stepwise therapy: ondansetron first, topical capsaicin adjunct, then only one monitored rescue agent under local CHS protocol; account for prior dystonia, QT risk and cumulative sedation.

guidance: Johns Hopkins All Children’s pediatric CHS pathway (updated August 2025); local adolescent medicine, toxicology, pharmacy and emergency pathways.
